# CHAPTER XVII.

## A preliminary investigation into the motion of the apogee and the nodes.

**T**his investigation will be as certain as the observations (indeed, the **PTOLEMAIC** traditions) are. Had it not been for this master [Ptolemy], we would know even less today about these very slow motions. Since the time that nations began to cultivate learning, no one else has been found who could help us here.

We assume here things found in **PTOLEMY** which are not entirely certain: First, that the fixed stars were precisely in those locations of the zodiac where they were placed by **PTOLEMY**. (Ptolemy, Book VII). Second, that the true <term>eccentricity</term> <note>The distance between the center of the circular orbit and the Sun.</note> of the Sun was what **PTOLEMY** reported: 415.5 parts, where the radius of the orbit is 100,000. (Ptolemy, Book III, Chapter IV). Third, that the <term>apogee</term> <note>The point furthest from the center of motion.</note> of the Sun remained at 5.5° of Gemini ♊. (Ibid.). Fourth, that the <term>apogee</term> of Mars (with its motion adjusted to the mean motion of the Sun) was found at 25.5° of Cancer ♋. (Ptolemy, Book X, Chapter VII). Fifth, that the <term>eccentricity</term> of Mars was 20,000 where the radius is 100,000. (Ibid.). Sixth, that the proportion of the <term>epicycle</term> <note>A small circle whose center moves along the circumference of a larger circle.</note> (according to **PTOLEMY**) or the <term>annual orbit</term> <note>The Earth's orbit around the Sun in the Copernican and Tychonic systems.</note> (according to **TYCHO** and **COPERNICUS**) to the orbit of Mars was as 100,000 to 151,900. Therefore, where the radius of the Sun's orbit or the "Great Orbit" is 100,000, the <term>eccentricity</term> of Mars will be 30,380. (Ptolemy, Book X, Chapter VIII).

We shall proceed as in Chapter 5.

<margin>[Geometric diagram with points A, B, C, d]</margin>

*Let A be the point from which the Great Orbit is described, C the equant point of Mars <note>An imaginary point used in ancient astronomy to account for the observed speeding up and slowing down of planets.</note>, and B the center of the Sun's orbit. And because AB is at 5.5° Gemini, and AC is at 25.5° Cancer, the angle CAB is 50°. AB is set at 415.5, while AC is 30,380 of those same parts. Given these two sides and the included angle, the angle CBA is found to be 123° 27'. And because BA points toward 5.5° Sagittarius, BC (after subtracting the angle 123° 27') will point toward approximately 2° 3' Leo ♌, and this was during the time of **PTOLEMY**. At the same time, CB, the <term>eccentricity of the equant</term> after transposition to the true motion of the Sun, was 18,353. Above this, from the transposition of the **TYCHONIC** hypothesis, I found 18,342: with one change, namely that instead of the size of the Martian orbit being 151,386, I used a more accurate 152,500. But this is in passing. Now to the matter at hand.*

# On the motion of the aphelia.

<margin>CHAPTER 16.</margin>
Because around the time of **Ptolemy** the <term>precession of the equinoxes</term> <note>The slow westward shift of the equinoxes along the ecliptic.</note> was deviating, no such suspicion remains clearly before or after that time. I will separate this, and examine the position of the <term>apsis</term> <note>The line connecting the closest and furthest points of an orbit.</note> relative to the Fixed stars. Moreover, the <term>Heart of the Lion</term> <note>The star Regulus.</note> was in that age at 2° 30' of Leo ♌. Therefore, the apogee of Mars, or its <term>aphelion</term> <note>The point in a planet's orbit furthest from the Sun.</note>, preceded this star by 27 minutes, around the year of **Christ** 140. In our age, **Tycho Brahe** found this star in the year of **Christ** 1587 at 24° 5' 30" of Leo ♌, while the aphelion had advanced to 28° 49' of Leo ♌, being distant from the Heart of the Lion by 4° 44' <term>in consequence</term> <note>Moving in the order of the signs, or eastward.</note>. If you add the previous 27 minutes to these, the sum (5 degrees 11 minutes) is the motion over the 1,447 intermediate years from the year of **Christ** 140 to 1587. The annual motion is therefore nearly 13 seconds; the motion over thirty years is 6' 29". If you again add to these the motion of the Fixed stars—or the **Tychonic** precession, which is almost uniform and the same for all times (the **Ptolemaic** alone excluded), namely 25 minutes 30 seconds for 30 years—you will produce the sum of 31' 59". Therefore, the annual motion of the aphelion of Mars from the equinox at this time is 1' 4".

# On the motion of the nodes.

For the sake of relatedness, we will now also settle this, though it is not so necessary. And because **Ptolemy**, in Book 13, Chapter 1, says that the <term>Northern Limit</term> <note>The point in the orbit furthest north of the ecliptic.</note> of Mars is <note>original: "περὶ τὰ τελευταῖα ♋ Καρκίνου, καὶ σχεδὸν περὶ τὸ ἀπογειότατον"</note> "around the end of Cancer ♋, and almost around the most distant point," let it then be in 29° of Cancer ♋, which is 3.5 degrees before the Heart of Leo ♌. Although **Ptolemy** in Book 3, Chapter 6, for the ease of calculation, places the Northern Limit in the very position of the apogee itself, namely in 25.5° of Cancer ♋. But today it is in about 16° 20' of Leo ♌, namely 7° 45' before the Heart of Leo ♌. Having subtracted 3° 30', it is discovered that the Northern Limit, and consequently the <term>nodes</term> <note>The two points where a planet's orbit crosses the plane of the Earth's orbit (the ecliptic).</note>, have receded from the Heart of Leo ♌ by 4° 15'. This is indeed consistent with the motions of the Moon, whose apogee likewise advances among the Fixed stars while its nodes recede. Therefore, the annual motion <term>in precedence</term> <note>Westward or retrograde motion.</note> is 10" 34"'; for 30 years it is 5' 17". Subtract these from the precession's motion of 25' 30". There remain 20' 13". And by just as many <term>scruples</term> <note>A term for small parts or minutes.</note>, the nodes of **Mars** in thirty current years are likewise moved from the equinoctial point <term>in consequence</term> <note>Eastward.</note>.

# CHAPTER XIX.

## Refutation of this hypothesis (which was established and proven through all locations) by means of acronychal latitudes, in accordance with the opinion of the authors.
->ACRONYCHAL.<-

<margin>
* In Saturn and Jupiter, he [Copernicus] simply bisected it—that is, he assigned the semi-diameter of the epicycle to a quadrant of the Copernican form. In Mars, however, although he had assigned a quadrant of the Ptolemaic eccentricity to the epicycle, and contended that in our age the entire Ptolemaic eccentricity had become smaller, he nevertheless left the epicycle its original size. Thus, he moved the center of the eccentric (to speak with Ptolemy) 40 units closer to the center of the annual orbit than to the center of the equant circle. Book 5, chapter 16. See also chapter 16 of this book.
</margin>

**W**ho would have thought it possible? This hypothesis, which agrees so closely with the acronychal <note>original Greek: ἀκρονύχιος</note> observations, is nevertheless false, whether the observations are examined in relation to the mean or the apparent position of the Sun. Ptolemy showed this to us when he taught that the eccentricity of the equant point <term>equant point<gloss>a mathematical point used by ancient astronomers to account for the observed speeding up and slowing down of planets</gloss></term> must be bisected by the center of the eccentric carrying the planet. For here, neither Tycho Brahe nor I bisected the eccentricity of the equant point.* Copernicus, indeed, made it a point of honor not to neglect this anywhere; for he used very few observations, perhaps thinking that Ptolemy had used no more than those reported in the *Great Work* <note>Ptolemy’s *Almagest*</note>. Tycho Brahe hesitated here. For, imitating Copernicus, he established the proportion of eccentricities that the acronychal observations required. But when not only the acronychal latitudes refuted this (for an increase from the second inequality still occurs in these), but also—and most especially—the observations of other configurations with the Sun affected by the second inequality, he stopped there and turned to Lunar matters, while I, in the meantime, arrived.

The METHOD, however, by which the entire theory of Mars would be easily completed if the preceding points were correct, and by which it is demonstrated that they are not correct, is as follows.

## PART TWO.

<margin>CHAPTER XIX.</margin>

FIRST, concerning the latitudes in the acronychal <term>acronychal<gloss>the position of a planet when it is in opposition to the Sun, appearing as the Sun sets</gloss></term> position. Let there be set out, in the Copernican form <note>the heliocentric arrangement where the Sun is the center of the system</note>, the line *DE* in the plane of the eccentric of Mars. On this line, let *A* be the Sun, *D* the Northern limit <term>limit<gloss>the point of maximum latitude, or greatest distance from the ecliptic plane</gloss></term>, and *E* the Southern limit, or the point closest to it. Through *A*, let the straight line *HL* be drawn, lying in the plane of the Earth's eccentric orbit. Now, let *AH* and *AD* be conceived as being in one plane of the circle of latitude; likewise *AL* and *AE*. Let the Earth in the year 1585 be on the line *AH*, specifically at point *B*; but in the year 1593, let it be on the line *AL* at point *C*.

Because *AB* and *AD* incline toward 21° Leo (where the Sun *A*, seen from the Earth at *B*, appears in 21° Aquarius), and conversely *E* and *C* incline toward 12° Pisces (where the Sun *A*, seen from the Earth at *C*, appears in 12° Virgo), and since 12° Virgo is closer to the Sun's apogee <term>apogee<gloss>the point where the Earth is furthest from the Sun</gloss></term> than 21° Aquarius, it follows that *BA* is shorter than *AC*.

I will extract these lines from page 98 of the first volume of **TYCHO BRAHE'S** *Progymnasmata* <note>Tycho's "Introduction to the New Astronomy," published posthumously in 1602</note> and assume they are correct, even though I will later demonstrate (led by the **METHOD**) that they are slightly different. There, *BA* is given as 97,500 and *AC* as 101,400. In the subsequent correction, *BA* will become a little longer and *AC* a little shorter, though they will not be equal. Now, because earlier in Chapter 13 (by two methods different from the present business) the angle *BAD* at the limit near 16° Leo was found to be about 1° 50', it is here, four or five degrees from the limit, 1° 49 1/2'. But the observed latitude *HBD* in the year 1585 was 4° 32' 10". Thus, with angles *HBD* and *BAD* given, their difference *BDA* is also given as 2° 42' 40". As the sine of *BDA* is to the known line *BA*, so is the sine of *BAD* to *DA*. If *BA* is assumed to be 97,500, *DA* comes out as 163,000. If it is 100,000, *DA* will be 167,200.

*Likewise, since C and E in the year 1593 are in Pisces, and Mars is 26 degrees from the limit and 6 1/4 degrees from the node; as the total sine is to the sine of the maximum inclination of 1° 50', so the sine of 6 1/4 is to the sine of CAE, the inclination at this location. Therefore, CAE is 1° 39'. But the observed latitude CE was 6° 3'. Therefore, the angle AEC is 4° 24'. Again, then, as the sine of AEC is to the known line AC, so the sine of ACE is to AE. If AC is assumed to be 101,400, AE comes out to nearly 139,300. If AC is 100,000, AE comes out to nearly 137,380.*

*Moreover, since 21° Leo is about eight degrees from the aphelion <term>aphelion<gloss>the point where Mars is furthest from the Sun</gloss></term>, the line AD at the aphelion itself will be about 150 units longer (which will be evident to anyone computing distances from the discovered hypothesis and translating them into these numbers), namely either 163,150 or 167,350. And since 12° Pisces is about 13 degrees from the perihelion <term>perihelion<gloss>the point where Mars is closest to the Sun</gloss></term>, AE at the perihelion itself will be about 300 units shorter, namely either 139,000 or 137,080. Thus we have the length of the lines AD and AE at the apsides themselves, when they are parts of the same straight line DE. Therefore, join DA 163,150 or 167,350*

->*And AE 139,000 or 137,080*<-
->*The total DE is therefore 302,150 or 304,430*<-
->*The half DK is 151,075 or 152,215*<-
->*Therefore the eccentricity AK is 12,075 or 15,135.*<-

*Let these numbers be translated into the former scale, where the radius of the eccentric was 100,000. Thus, as 151,075 is to 100,000, so 12,075 is to 8,000;*
*Or as 152,215 is to 100,000, so 15,135 is to 9,943.*

The eccentricity <term>eccentricity<gloss>the measurement of how much an orbit deviates from a perfect circle</gloss></term> of the eccentric is therefore most truly found (using the acronychal <term>acronychal<gloss>referring to observations made when a planet is in opposition to the Sun, appearing in the sky as the Sun sets</gloss></term> latitudes as indicators) to be between 8,000 and 9,943, where the radius of the eccentric orbit is 100,000. But our hypothesis, constructed from the acronychal observations of longitudes, produced an eccentricity for the eccentric of 11,332—very different from the value between 8,000 and 9,943, which sits almost in the middle. Therefore, it must be that something we had assumed is false. Now, what was assumed was this: that the orbit through which the planet passes is a perfect circle; and that there is some unique point on the line of apsides <term>line of apsides<gloss>the line extending through the center of an orbit connecting the points of greatest and least distance</gloss></term> at a certain and constant distance from the center of the eccentric, around which point Mars completes equal angles in equal times <note>Kepler is referring to the "equant," a mathematical device used by Ptolemy to explain varying speeds of planets</note>. Therefore, either one or perhaps both of these assumptions are false. For the observations employed are not false.

This same demonstration also holds against that hypothesis which is established by observations reduced to the mean motion of the Sun: because the latitudes remain nearly the same during the time between both points. For those observations, the eccentricity of the eccentric is shown to be 9,943, which nonetheless was assumed above in Chapter V from the restoration by **BRAHE** <note>Tycho Brahe, the Danish astronomer whose data Kepler was using</note> to be 12,600, or in the **PTOLEMAIC** equant as 12,352, where the total eccentricity of the point of the equant is 20,160 or 19,763.

### For the transformation of our diagram to the PTOLEMAIC form

*Let **DE** be the line of apsides, **A** the earth, **D. E.** the center of the epicycle <term>epicycle<gloss>a small circle whose center moves around the circumference of a larger one, used in ancient astronomy to explain planetary motion</gloss></term> at the highest and lowest apside: and from points **D** and **E**, let straight lines be drawn toward the earth **A** parallel to the plane of the ecliptic **BC**: in which let **DF** and **EG**, the radii of the epicycle, be taken as equal to **BA** and **AC**: and the planet at **F** and **G**. Therefore, the inclination **FDA** was equal to the inclination **BAD**, and the line of sight **AF** is parallel to the previous **BD**. Wherefore both **DAF** and **HBD** show the same observed latitude. The same must be said regarding the congruent triangles **ACE** and **EGA**. Thus, the demonstration and the quantities of the corresponding lines are the same.*

The reader may wonder why I make the semi-diameter of the epicycle of Mars unequal to itself—namely, making **DF** equal to the longer **BA**, and **EG** equal to the shorter **CA**. I respond, based on the first part of this work, that this happens because of the transposition of observations from opposition with the mean Sun to opposition with the apparent Sun <note>Kepler was a pioneer in arguing that planetary orbits should be calculated relative to the actual physical Sun, rather than the "mean Sun," which was a mathematical average</note>. But if we remain with the mean motion of the Sun (for the present argument holds even then), **DF** and **EG** will remain equal, at least up to this point. But see Chapter VI of the first part regarding this.

*For the **BRAHEAN** form, leaving one or the other triangle—suppose **DBA**, so that **B** is the immobile earth, and **A** is the Sun in the year 1585—let **AB** be continued so that **BH** is equal to **AC**: and let **H** be the Sun in the year 1603 in 12° Virgo: and let **HI** be made equal and parallel to **AE** in the same directions, so that Mars is at perigee <term>perigee<gloss>the point in an orbit where the planet is closest to the Earth</gloss></term> in **I**, and at apogee <term>apogee<gloss>the point furthest from the Earth</gloss></term> in **D**; the ecliptic is **HBA**; the inclination **BHI**, **BAD**: the perigee latitude **IBA**, the apogee latitude **DBH**. Again, therefore, the sum of **DA** and **HI** will come out the same, of which **DK** is the half and **KA** is the eccentricity.* The only difference is this, that for **PTOLEMY** the plane of the epi-

...of the epicycle; for TYCHO, the plane of the eccentric <term>eccentric<gloss>the circular path of a planet when its center is placed away from the Sun or Earth</gloss></term> is shifted from North to South and back again, while remaining parallel to itself; in COPERNICUS, both remain in the same position.

Meanwhile, note this too. I had found the composite eccentricity in Chapter 16 to be 18,564. Its half, 9,282, is almost exactly in the middle between the values 8,000 and 9,943. But PTOLEMY had also taught us (as was said above) that half of the value found from the acronychal <term>acronychal<gloss>referring to observations made when a planet is in opposition to the Sun</gloss></term> positions should be assigned to the eccentricity of the eccentric. But conversely, if we bisect the discovered 18,564, we will represent the acronychal positions around the middle longitudes of the eccentric quite precisely, but not equally so for the positions around the octants <term>octants<gloss>points in the orbit 45 degrees away from the apsides</gloss></term> and toward the apsides <term>apsides<gloss>the points where the planet is closest to or farthest from the center of motion</gloss></term>.

*For example, consider the opposition of the year 1593. The simple anomaly <term>anomaly<gloss>the angle measuring the planet's progress around its orbit from its furthest point</gloss></term> in the preceding chapter was 6 signs, 11 degrees, 3 minutes, 16 seconds <note>Kepler uses a system where a circle is divided into 12 "signs" of 30 degrees each</note>. I multiply the sine of 11° 3' 16", namely 19,174, by 9,282. Previously, it had to be multiplied by 7,232. This yields a sine of 1,780 for an arc of 1° 1' 12", which is a part of the equation. When added to 11° 3' 16", it produces a semi-equated anomaly of 6 signs, 12 degrees, 4 minutes, 28 seconds. Its complement is 167° 55' 32"; the half of that is 83° 57' 46". Its tangent, about 945,500, multiplied by the perihelion distance 90,718 and divided in turn by the aphelion distance 109,282, produces a tangent of 784,880. Its arc, 82° 44' 20", subtracted from the prior 83° 57' 46", leaves 1° 13' 26" for the other part of the equation. This, added to the semi-equated anomaly, and that to the aphelion <term>aphelion<gloss>the point in the orbit furthest from the Sun</gloss></term>, places the planet at 12° 13' 37" of Pisces: where it differs from the previous hypothesis by three minutes, and becomes further removed from the actual observation. For it should have been 12 degrees 16 minutes of Pisces.*

This appears more clearly at 17° Cancer in the year 1582. For when the bisection is applied, Mars falls at 17° 4 3/4' Cancer, and this calculation differs from ours by 7 1/2 minutes at about the 45th degree from the aphelion, but from observation it differs by 9 minutes.

<margin>
* In the prosthaphæreses <term>prosthaphæreses<gloss>the geometric corrections added or subtracted to the mean motion to find the true position</gloss></term> of the annual orbit, however, those 8 minutes of error occasionally grow as large as 30 minutes.
</margin>
And from this very small difference of eight minutes, the reason is clear why PTOLEMY, since he needed the bisection, settled for a stable equatory point <note>The "equant," a point around which the planet's motion was assumed to be uniform</note>. For if the eccentricity of the equant—as much as the maximum equations around the middle longitudes undoubtedly allow—is bisected, you see that the greatest error of all from observation amounts to 8 minutes, and that in Mars, whose eccentricity is the greatest; it would therefore be less in the others. But PTOLEMY professes that he does not descend below 10 minutes, or a sixth part of a degree, in his observations. Therefore, the uncertainty or (as they say) the "latitude" of the observations exceeds the error of this Ptolemaic calculation.

Since divine kindness has granted us TYCHO BRAHE, a most diligent observer, by whose observations this 8-minute error of the PTOLEMAIC calculation in Mars is proven; it is right that we both acknowledge and cultivate this gift of GOD with a grateful mind. Let us indeed labor so that we may finally track down the genuine form of celestial motions (supported by these arguments of detected false suppositions). In this path I will go before others in the following pages according to my small measure. For if I had thought 8 minutes of longitude were to be ignored, I would already have corrected...

### CHAPTER XX.

### Refutation of that same hypothesis by observations made outside of acronychal positions.

**NOW** I shall proceed to a second argument by which the "eccentric eccentricity" <note>original: "eccentrica eccentricitas"</note> found in Chapter 17 is shown to be false (notwithstanding the fact that it provides the true motions in longitude): namely, by using observations of other configurations with the Sun made outside of <term>oppositions<gloss>when Mars is directly opposite the Sun from Earth's perspective</gloss></term>, specifically when the planet was observed while moving near the <term>apsides<gloss>the points where the planet is closest to or farthest from the Sun</gloss></term> of the <term>eccentric<gloss>the circular path of the planet</gloss></term>.

In the year 1600, on March 5/15, around midnight, Mars was seen at 29° 12' 30'' in Cancer (♋) with a latitude of 3° 23' North. Its mean longitude, corrected by our addition, was 4 signs, 29° 14' 58''; its <term>aphelion<gloss>the point in the orbit furthest from the Sun</gloss></term> was at 4 signs, 29° 2' 45''. Therefore, the <term>anomaly<gloss>the angle measuring the planet's progress around its orbit from its furthest point</gloss></term> was 0° 12' 13''. This requires an <term>equation<gloss>a correction added or subtracted to the mean motion to find the true position</gloss></term> of 2' to be subtracted, according to the hypothesis of eccentric positions established above. Therefore, the eccentric position of Mars was at 29° 13' Cancer; the Sun's position was at 25° 45' 51'' Aries (♈).

*In the diagram, let A be the Sun, B Mars, and C Earth. Therefore, by subtracting the direction of the Earth from Mars (CB = 29° 12' 30'' Cancer) from the direction of the Sun to Mars (AB = 29° 13' Cancer), the angle CBA will be 0° 30' 30''. By subtracting the direction of the Sun from the Earth (CA = 25° 45' 51'' Aries) from the direction of Mars from the Earth (CB = 29° 12' 30'' Cancer), the angle BCA will be 123° 26' 39''. Now, as the sine of angle CBA is to the side CA, so is the sine of angle BCA to the side BA. However, CA (the distance of the Sun from the Earth according to Tycho's tables) is 99,302 (which, although slightly flawed, the true value lies within 100,000, as we shall hear below in Chapter 30). Therefore, the distance AB is between 165,680 and 166,846.*

Let us take an observation at <term>perihelion<gloss>the point in the orbit closest to the Sun</gloss></term>, which was held in the year 1593 on July 30, at 1:45 AM the following night. Mars was found at 17° 39' Aries (♈) with a latitude of 6° 6' 15'' South. The mean longitude of Mars was 1 sign, 26° 16' 38''. The aphelion was at 4 signs, 28° 55' 43''. Therefore, Mars is distant from the perihelion by 2° 39' 5'', to which an equation of 32' to be subtracted corresponds, according to the hypothesis found above, so that the eccentric position of Mars is 1 sign, 25° 44' 30'', and the apparent position of the Sun is 17° 3' 0'' Leo (♌).

*In the diagram, let BA be extended to D; let AD be at 25° 44' 30'' Aquarius (♒), and ED at 17° 39' 30'' Aries (♈). Therefore, angle EDA is 21° 55' 0''. And because ED is at 17° 39' 30'' Aries, and EA is at 17° 3' Leo, the angle AED is 149° 23' 30''. As the sine of angle EDA is to side EA, so is the sine of angle AED to side AD. Now, EA (the distance of the Sun from the Earth from Tycho's table) is 102,689—flawed indeed, but certainly greater than 100,000. Therefore, the distance AD is between 140,080 and 136,409.*

*Let the line B A D be set out in the plane of the ecliptic, and through A, which denotes the Sun or the center of the world, let the straight line L A M be drawn in the plane of the orbit, so that the star is at L and M. Let the Earth be at C, and the triangle C A B be part of the plane of the ecliptic, to which plane the triangle L B A is understood to be perpendicular: and let points C, L, and B be connected; and let the lines be continued to the surface of the sphere of the Fixed Stars, A B at $\beta$, A L at $\lambda$, and A C at $\nu$. Let $\nu \beta$ be the arc of the ecliptic, $\beta \lambda$ the arc of the circle of latitude, and $\nu \lambda$ the transverse arc. Therefore, the observation of the star's position among the Fixed Stars is referred to the ecliptic by transferring the arc of the circle of latitude to the ecliptic $\nu \beta$ perpendicularly through the observed position of the star: and the triangle C L B is part of the plane of that circle. But $\lambda \beta$ is also placed as a circle of latitude perpendicular to the ecliptic $\nu \beta$. Therefore, the planes of two circles perpendicular to the same ecliptic (C L B and L B A) intersect each other along the line L B. Therefore, by [Proposition] XIX of the eleventh book of **EUCLID**, the line of intersection L B will be perpendicular to the plane of the ecliptic C B A and its line B A; that is, L B A will be a right angle. Having found the length B A in the ecliptic, therefore, and knowing the angle L A B <note>This angle represents the inclination of Mars's orbit relative to the Earth's orbit</note>, the sought-after length L A cannot remain unknown. This is what was to be done.*

In the present business, then, since the inclination or angle L A B is $1^{\circ} 48'$ in this place, L A in the present dimension is longer by 82 parts than E A, and A M is longer by 72 than A D.

# CHAPTER 21.

## The cause why a false hypothesis produces the truth, and to what extent?

**F**URTHERMORE, because I vehemently hate that axiom of the <term>Logicians<gloss>Kepler uses the term 'Dialecticians,' referring to those who study formal logic and argument</gloss></term>, <note>original: "EX FALSO VERUM SEQUI"</note> **TRUTH FOLLOWS FROM THE FALSE**, because it is used to attack the throat of **COPERNICUS** (whom I follow as my master in the more universal hypotheses of the system of the world): I thought it worth the reader’s effort to show how the truth follows from the false in this case.

First, you have already seen that the result is not entirely true. For while the path of a planet through one plane of the <term>eccentric<gloss>the off-center circle used in astronomy to model how planets appear to speed up and slow down</gloss></term> is considered in two ways—namely, both by reason of its <term>longitude<gloss>its position in degrees along the zodiac</gloss></term> at certain degrees and minutes of the zodiacal circle, and by reason of its altitude or distance from the center of the world around which it travels (which shows different values at different places in the zodiac)—our false assumption indeed brought the planet to its proper places in longitude at the proper times, but it did not provide it with its proper altitude. Therefore, the complete truth did not follow from this false hypothesis.

Secondly, the effect of both the true (yet still unknown) hypothesis and the false one we adopted is not the same (even regarding longitude alone) simply because the effect *seems* the same to our senses. For it is possible for some tiny detail to be missing that the senses cannot grasp.

I will now demonstrate the **CIRCUMSTANCES** by which it can happen that a false hypothesis mimics a true one within the limits of sensory precision regarding longitude.

*Let the straight line **MP** be projected through the center of the world **A** into opposite parts of the zodiac, say into 29 degrees of Leo (♌) and Aquarius (♒). And let it be that, by some true hypothesis, the planet moves for half of its time between the lines **AM** and **AP** on the left, and for the remaining half on the right, so that it is always on the alternating lines (**AM**, **AP**) after half of its period of return: and this particular effect of the true hypo-* <note>The text cuts off here, continuing the word 'hypothesis' on the next page.</note>

<margin>CAP. XX. <note>Though the margin reads Chapter 20, this text continues the argument of Chapter 21 regarding the "truth following from the false."</note></margin>
...may be expressed through some other invented <term>hypothesis<gloss>a mathematical model or "working guess" about the shape and speed of a planet's orbit</gloss></term>.
Thus, let whatever circle or other winding path be drawn with its center taken on the line MP, provided that it encompasses the center of the world, A, and is bisected into two equal parts by the line MP. The goal will be achieved, with the planet traversing the circle with <term>equable motion<gloss>moving at a constant speed, covering equal angles in equal times</gloss></term> (which is regular around some point on the line MP, whether that point be fixed or wandering). For example, if circle OP is drawn around center A and moves uniformly. There is, therefore, something common to all these circles and other figures by which the desired result is obtained, namely this: that they surround the center of the world and move regularly around some point on the line MP. Now, this or that figure or circle, and this or that point of equality, can be false among those things which are included under the same category. Yet we achieved what was proposed, not through this false specific form, but through the general truth that was present in this adopted false form.

Let us now proceed, and suppose that after the <term>quadrants of time<gloss>the points in time exactly halfway between the planet's closest and furthest approach to the Sun</gloss></term>, the planet is positioned on the lines AM, AK, AP, and AL, where the angles MAK and MAL are less than right angles. In this case, the previous circle OP will wander off at the sides. For because it was assumed to be regular around center A, if a straight line VX is drawn through A perpendicular to MP, then MAV and MAX would become the measures of the quadrants of time. Consequently, this hypothesis would place the planet on the lines AV and AX, whereas it ought to be on AK and AL.

And since experience witnesses that the motions of the planets most certainly strive after circles (even if they perhaps do not fully attain them), and the nature of such motions is to intensify and slacken gradually, admitting nothing sudden; therefore, the error of this hypothesis of circle OP will begin little by little from line AM, then increase more and more and become greatest at AK, and again gradually vanish at AP. Thus, the uniform and <term>concentric<gloss>a circle whose center is the same as the center of the world—in this case, the Sun</term> hypothesis OP will nowhere fail more than at AK and AL, with the angles KAV and LAX being 10 1/2 degrees in the case of Mars.

LET THERE BE, THEN, another hypothesis, which also shows us the lines AK and AL. But again, there can be various hypotheses that achieve this. For we could connect the points where AK and AL intersect the circle OP; and where this straight line intersects the line MP, we could place the point of equality for the motion of circle OP, so that the motion of circle OP becomes unequal; then we would also obtain the lines AK and AL. But because a certain <term>genius<gloss>Kepler refers here to a guiding spirit or a natural inclination of the mind toward elegance</gloss></term> commands us to choose the simplest and most uniform things, we shall therefore seek a circle that moves uniformly around its own center, which will achieve what is proposed for us. Thus, having established equal parts on AK and AL starting from A—namely, AK and AL—let the points K and L be connected by a straight line intersecting MP at C. Then, with center C and the distance CK, let an <term>eccentric circle<gloss>a circle whose center is shifted away from the Sun's position</gloss></term> MN be drawn, whose motion is regular around the center. This hypothesis will represent the planet in its proper place on the four lines AM, AN, AK, and AL. Yet not only this hypothesis, but many others could do this, because they possess this general and indeed very true principle:

...so that the point of equality of motion <note>original: punctum æqualitatis motus; this is the "equant point," a mathematical point from which the planet's speed appears constant</note> is on the line that connects the locations of the planet falling on the lines AK and AL, and at that point where this line cuts MP. <margin>CHAPTER XXII. <note>Though the margin identifies this as Chapter 22, Kepler is continuing the geometric proof regarding the reduction of error within the same logical progression.</note></margin>

Therefore, having bisected the angles MCK and KCN, let two new lines be drawn through C, cutting the circumference at Q, T, R, and S: the maximum error, if any exists, will be around these points. This hypothesis will then represent the planet around the eighths of the times on the lines AQ, AR, AS, and AT. Suppose now (as is the case with Mars) that the planet ought not to appear in the lines AQ, AR, AS, AT after eighths of the <term>restorative time<gloss>the time it takes for a planet to return to the same point in its orbit</gloss></term>: but rather there in the higher lines AF and AE, and here in the lower ones AG and AD. Therefore, if the error KAV was previously 10 ½ degrees, now the error KAF will hardly be a few <term>scruples<gloss>minutes of arc; 1/60th of a degree</gloss></term>. In the case of Mars, the angle QAF or RAE is found to be about 9 minutes, but SAG or TAD is about 28 minutes.

THIRDLY, therefore, let this hypothesis also be corrected. Just as this can be done in various ways (specifically by the <term>libration<gloss>a back-and-forth oscillating motion</gloss></term> of point *c* on line GA), so too are we hindered by no religious scruple <note>Kepler uses "religione" here to mean a binding rule or hesitation</note> from keeping the point of equality *c* fixed at the distance CA because of the angle KAV, while still keeping the path of the planet circular. These three things, assumed by choice and not proven by demonstration, will force us to lower the center of the eccentric from point *c* (the point of equality of motion) to point B, so that the line HI replaces MN, and the body of the planet departs from Q, R, S, and T. While remaining on the lines CQ, CR, CS, and CT (because the measurement of time remains at C), let it come into the marks F, E, G, and D. Let the segments QF, ER, SG, and TD be of such a size that QAF and EAR become 9 minutes, and SAG and TAD become 28 minutes. 

With this done, even that error in the eighths of the times will have been absorbed, and the hypothesis will exhibit the most accurate longitude in eight locations. Wherefore, if any error remains again, it will be in the <term>sixteenths of the times<gloss>points representing 1/16th of the orbital period</gloss></term>, in the intermediate locations. But because this third eccentric HI is as equivalent to the first in the locations AM and AP as it is to the second in the locations AK and AL, it therefore introduces no new error. And because the error of the second model was greatest in the eighths of the times (which has now been absorbed), there will remain in the sixteenths a much smaller error from the old error. If we use a proportion: just as the error of the first eccentric was 10 ½ degrees and the error of the second was 9 or 28 minutes—namely, a seventieth and a twenty-fifth part of the former—now let us again make the second errors of the third models many times smaller: clearly...

## PART TWO

...we have constrained the matter within the failure of the senses <note>original: "intra sensuum defectum," referring to the margin of error in human observation before the invention of the telescope</note> even concerning the sixteenths of time <note>the points in the orbit representing 1/16th of the total period</note>.

<margin>Chapter XXI. <note>The previous page margin noted Chapter 22, but the text continues the logic of the vicarious hypothesis. Early printed editions of Kepler often have inconsistent chapter numbering in the margins.</note></margin>
THUS IT IS ALREADY clear to what extent and in what way truth follows from false principles: namely, that which is false in these principles is specific and can be absent; but that which brings necessity to the truth is, under a general reckoning, entirely true in itself.

Finally, just as these false principles are only suitable at certain places throughout the entire circle: so truth does not follow in every way outside of those very places, except insofar as it happens in this business that the difference can no longer be estimated by the sensitivity of the senses.

AND THIS same dullness of the senses also covers this tiny error which remains in the eighths of the times <note>points at 45, 135, 225, and 315 degrees from the starting point</note>. That it remains, I demonstrate thus:

*For if from B a perfect <term>eccentric<gloss>a circular orbit whose center is not at the Sun</gloss></term> is again drawn, so that BD, BE, BF, and BG are equal; and we make BC of such a size that the required angle QAF exists: then it is not indeed left to our choice how large we want the angle SAG to appear. For it becomes entirely necessary. Let the perpendicular AZ fall from A onto QT. Let AC (as above) be 18,564, of which CQ is 100,000. And because angle ACZ is 45°, AZ or ZC (each of these parts) will become 13,127. Therefore ZQ is 113,127, and angle AQZ is 6° 37' 5", and QAZ is 83° 22' 55", the tangent of which is 864,092. However, let FAZ be taken as 9 <term>scruples<gloss>minutes of a degree</gloss></term> smaller. Its tangent FL will be 844,900. But where AZ is 13,127, ZF will be 110,910. Therefore QF is 2,217. However, QF is larger than TD, which I demonstrate thus: QT is the diameter of the circle. It is therefore equal to the joined <term>semidiameters<gloss>radii</gloss></term> FB and BD. But BF and BD, taken together, are larger than FD. Therefore QT is also larger than FD. Let the common part FT be taken away. The remaining part QF is therefore larger than TD. And yet we will allow it to be equal out of abundance. Let CZ (13,127) be subtracted from CT, so that ZT remains 86,873. Therefore, from AZ and ZT, angle ATZ is known, and it is 8° 35' 33". Therefore ZAT is 81° 24' 27". And because ZT is 86,873, I will add to it the equal of QF, as if it were TD, namely 2,217. ZD becomes 89,090. But where AZ is 100,000, ZD will become the tangent of angle ZAD, which is 686,291. Thus this angle is 81° 42' 35". But ZAT was 81° 24' 27". Therefore TAD or SAG is less than 18' 8" in difference, because TD is smaller than 2,217.*

Behold here the necessary angle TAD, which ought to have been 27 1/3 minutes. Thus, if you make QAF 12 minutes instead of 9, TAD becomes 24. And on both sides, the Planet will become 3 minutes higher than is right. The <term>equation<gloss>the correction applied to the mean motion to find the true position</gloss></term> will therefore seem too large; for which reason the eccentricity is too large. It will therefore be decreased a little, so that in lines AK and AL, the Planet becomes about 1 1/2 minutes lower, and in DE and FG, just as many (namely 1 1/2) minutes higher.

So, through this balancing of various causes, it happens that with one error compensating for another, the calculation is brought within the sensitivity of the senses, and the falsity of the specific <term>hypothesis<gloss>the mathematical model of the orbit</gloss></term> cannot be detected. Therefore, this cunning little whore <note>original: "vafra meretricula," a surprisingly salty metaphor for a mathematical model that gives the right answer for the wrong reasons</note> cannot boast of truth (that most modest maiden) <note>original: "pudicissima puella"</note> having been dragged into her brothel <note>original: "lupanar"</note>. A certain honest woman was closely following a prostitute who went before her because of the narrowness of the streets and the crowd of people: whom the foolish and bleary-eyed professors of logical subtleties, who...

<summary>Kepler uses a geometric proof to show that his "vicarious hypothesis" produces errors of only a few minutes of arc at the "eighths" of the orbit. He argues that the model's apparent accuracy is actually the result of several errors canceling each other out, famously comparing the model to a "cunning prostitute" mimicking the truth.</summary>

<meta>This page concludes Part Two of Kepler's New Astronomy. Having spent chapters developing a "vicarious hypothesis" (a mathematical model that accurately predicts the position of Mars but fails to provide the correct distances from the Sun), Kepler now formally admits that this model, while sophisticated and based on the methods of his predecessors Ptolemy, Copernicus, and Brahe, is physically impossible. He is preparing the reader for Part Three, where he will seek the physical causes of planetary motion.</meta>

...cannot distinguish an honest face from a brazen one <note>original: "frontem ingenuam a perfricata," a classical idiom contrasting a modest, blushing forehead with one "rubbed" smooth and incapable of blushing out of shame</note>, they have judged her to be the handmaid of a harlot.

<margin>Chapter XXI. <note>In the original printing, this concludes the demonstration from the previous pages regarding the subtle errors in the vicarious hypothesis.</note></margin>
**AND THIS** is undoubtedly the reason why, in Chapter 18, in the signs of Leo and Libra and everywhere else, there is still a discrepancy of a minute or two <note>original: "scrupulum," referring to a minute of arc, a tiny measurement equivalent to 1/60th of a degree</note>. But the error could not be easily detected, since the observations used do not fall exactly on the apsides <term>apsides<gloss>the points in an orbit where the planet is closest to or farthest from the center of its motion</gloss></term> or on the quarters and eighths of the orbital periods <note>the points marking 90 and 45 degrees of travel along the orbital circle</note>.

### CONCLUSION OF THE SECOND PART.

**HITHERTO**, therefore, the hypothesis serving the first inequality <note>the variation in a planet’s speed caused by its eccentric path, rather than its alignment with Earth</note> has been transferred (in which **BRAHE** agrees with **COPERNICUS**, though both differ somewhat in form from **PTOLEMY**) from the mean motion of the Sun—which all three authors used—to the apparent motion of the Sun. **THEN** it was shown that whether we follow the apparent motion of the Sun and the hypothesis found in Chapter 16, or the mean motion of the Sun <note>Kepler is moving astronomy away from "mean motion"—an imaginary averaged speed—to the "apparent" or true position of the Sun as the center of the system</note> and the hypothesis proposed in Chapter 8 from the restoration by **BRAHE**, in both cases there follow false distances of the planet from the center, whether that center be the Sun (for **COPERNICUS** and **BRAHE**) or the world <note>the Earth</note> (for **PTOLEMY**). Therefore, what we had previously built up from **BRAHE’S** observations, we have later torn down again using other observations from the same man. This happened to us of necessity, because we followed certain things that were probable but in reality false, in imitation of the earlier masters.

## CHAPTER XXII.

### The epicycle, or the annual orbit, is not situated uniformly around the point of equality of motion.

In this manner, our **PREDECESSORS** first measured the <term>first inequality</term> <note>The variation in a planet's speed that occurs as it moves along its own path, regardless of where the Earth is.</note>. Later, having established a calculation that represented the planet's <term>eccentric</term> <note>A circular path where the center of the circle is not the center of the Earth or the Sun.</note> position at any given moment, they turned to investigating the <term>second inequality</term> <note>The apparent variation in a planet's speed or direction—like retrograde motion—caused by the observer's own movement on Earth.</note> (which depends upon the Sun). They did this by comparing the observed or apparent position with the position assigned by the eccentric and the first inequality alone.

However, as I traveled this same path, a doubtful fork in the road appeared to me in the previous Chapters 19 and 20, and the observations (those most faithful guides) were found to be at odds with other observations. I had to think about a completely different way of organizing the journey, according to the **M E T H O D** that follows.

**F I R S T**, in this third part, I will tackle the second inequality. Through undeniable observations, I will demonstrate, confirm, or refute those things which I have hitherto placed among my principles, though with hesitant assent. For once this "key" is found, the rest will lie open. **A F T E R W A R D**, in the fourth part, I shall approach the first inequality.

In the **COSMOGRAPHIC MYSTERY** <note>original: "Mysterio Cosmographico," Kepler’s first major book published in 1596.</note>, Chapter 22, when I was rendering the physical cause of the **PTOLEMAIC** <term>equant</term> <note>A mathematical point used to explain why planets seem to speed up or slow down; motion around this point is uniform in angle, but not in distance.</note> or the **COPERNICAN-TYCHONIC** second epicycle, I raised an objection to myself at the end of the chapter: if the cause I provided were genuine, it ought to be valid across all planets. However, since the **E A R T H**, being one of the stars (according to Copernicus), or the **S U N** (according to the others), has not hitherto required this equant, I decided that this speculation should remain uncertain until it became clearer to astronomers. Nevertheless, I harbored a suspicion that even this theory would have its own equant. After I came to know **TYCHO BRAHE**, this suspicion was confirmed in me. For **B R A H E**, in a letter sent to me in Styria in the year 1598, wrote these words:

> *The annual orbit according to Copernicus, or the epicycle according to Ptolemy, does not seem to be always of the same size when compared to the eccentric itself; rather, it introduces a sensible alteration in all three superior planets, to such an extent that the angle of difference in Mars grows to one degree and 45 minutes.*

At the same time, he touched upon this same point in the appendix to his *Mechanica* or in the narrative of his studies. He used similar words in Volume 1 of his letters, page 209, where he thinks that because of the Sun's eccentricity, a certain inequality is also mixed into the equations and <term>acronychal positions</term> <note>original: "sitibus acronychiis," the positions of a planet when it is directly opposite the Sun in the sky, rising just as the Sun sets.</note> of the eccentric. This was indeed refuted in the first part—that it does not overflow into the acronychal positions, or at least only very minimally—yet it seems it should be understood as a certain correction regarding the square-alignments of Mars with the Sun.

The center of the planetary system is the common intersection of the lines that are drawn through the <term>apsides</term> <note>The points in an orbit where a planet is closest to or farthest from the center of its motion.</note> of the individual planets. And that point is either very near the body of the Sun, as **BRAHE** initially preferred, or in the center of the Sun itself, as **I** correct it.
</margin>

**EVEN BACK THEN**, when I heard that the annual orbit was said to increase and decrease, my inner genius dictated to me that this "phantom" arose from the fact that **COPERNICUS’S** annual orbit (or **PTOLEMY’S** <term>epicycle</term> <note>A small circle whose center moves around the circumference of a larger one; used in ancient astronomy to explain planetary loops.</note>) is not at an equal distance from that center around which it is assumed to complete equal angles in equal times. For what physical cause would make the circuit of the center of the planetary <term>system</term> (for **TYCHO**) or the circuit of the **EARTH** (for **COPERNICUS**) or the **EPICYCLE** carrying the star (for **PTOLEMY**) increase and decrease? What is this, I say, but a novelty without example in Astronomy, an absurdity without probability?

Rather, it was more reasonable to believe that in some places the Sun (for **COPERNICUS**), the center of the planetary system (for **TYCHO**), or the body of the planet (for **PTOLEMY**) is farther from the chosen point of equality, and in other places closer—and this undoubtedly occurs on the line of apsides. A convenient opportunity for this seemed to be provided by my suspicion derived from my *Cosmographic Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterio meo Cosmographico," Kepler's first major work published in 1596.</note>, namely, if an <term>equant</term> <note>A mathematical point used to explain the observed non-uniform speed of planetary motion while maintaining the idea of circular paths.</note> were introduced into the theory of the **SUN** (or the theory of the Ptolemaic epicycle, so to speak).

Let us assume that the second inequality begins from the line of the Sun’s <term>mean motion</term> <note>The average speed of a planet, as if it moved in a perfect circle at a constant rate.</note>, as has pleased **ASTRONOMERS** until now (so that no one suspects my innovation in using the Sun's apparent motion in this business). And in the present diagram, let the <term>eccentricity</term> <note>The distance the center of a planet's orbit is offset from the center of the Sun or Earth.</note> of the planet for **COPERNICUS** arise not from the center of the Sun **A**, but from point **C**, around which the motion of the **EARTH** is assumed to be regular. Let that point **C** be not the center of the terrestrial orbit **DE**, but only the center of equality, being farther from the Sun **A** than the center of the terrestrial orbit **B** is from **A**. I say that if these things are granted, observations will be produced from which one might suspect that the annual orbit **DE** increases and decreases.

Let a perpendicular line be drawn from **C** to **DE**, which is **CF**. Let the star **MARS** be at **F** twice: once when the **EARTH** is at **D** and once when it is at **E**. Let **F** be connected with points **D** and **E**. Therefore, because **C** is the point of the Earth's equal motion on **DE**, the angles **FCD** and **FCE** will be the <term>anomaly of commutation</term> <note>The angle used to calculate a planet's parallax, or its change in apparent position due to the Earth's movement.</note>, and (as we assume) equal on both sides. Now, if **CD** and **CE** were equal (as has been thought until now), then the angles **DFC** and **EFC**—the <term>parallaxes</term> <note>The apparent displacement of an object when viewed from two different positions.</note> of the orbit—would be equal on both sides at each anomaly of commutation. But because **CE** is greater than **CD**, the angle **CFE** will also appear greater than angle **CFD**. Therefore, an observer who does not realize that this enlargement happens only at **E** (or nearby places), and the corresponding decrease happens only at the opposite location **D**, will judge that the entire annual orbit sometimes becomes larger (measured by **CE**) and sometimes narrower (measured by **CD**). This happens because such a person, following traditional Astronomy, presupposes that point **C** of equal motion is also the center of the circle **DE**.

In the **PTOLEMAIC** form, let the **EARTH** be at **C**. Let the lines of the Sun’s mean motion be **CK** and **CL**, representing what were previously **DC** and **EC** for **COPERNICUS**. And let the center around which the epicyclic motion is regular be at **F**, and let **IH** be equal and parallel to **ED**...

<summary>Kepler argues that the Earth's orbit (the annual orbit) does not have a single fixed center, but rather an "equant" point from which its motion appears uniform, similar to other planets. He demonstrates through geometry that ignoring this eccentricity leads astronomers to wrongly conclude that the orbit itself is physically expanding or contracting.</summary>

<margin>* Note this unexpected thing <note>original: ἀπροσδόκητον</note> for me. *For to hide the true cause of this diversity—namely, to free the eccentricity of the <term>SUN</term> from suspicion—it helps much that in this way the distance c k (from the center of the system to the <term>EARTH</term>) is short where the distance c e (from the <term>SUN</term> to the <term>EARTH</term>) is long; and conversely, that distance c l is long where c d is short.*

*The cause of the <term>apsides</term> <note>The points of greatest or least distance in an orbit.</note> being turned in this manner is as follows: In the <term>COPERNICAN</term> <note>The system of Nicolaus Copernicus, where the Earth and planets orbit the Sun.</note> model, the Earth travels through parts opposite to those of the <term>TYCHONIC</term> Sun and the <term>PTOLEMAIC</term> epicycle. **THEREFORE, IN ORDER** to either confirm or refute this speculation with observations, I entered upon this path. Since the <term>apogee</term> <note>The point in an orbit farthest from the center of motion.</note> of the SUN is at 5½° Leo [♌], I asked whether an observation existed where <term>Mars</term> [♂], by reason of its <term>first inequality</term> <note>The variation in a planet's speed caused by its own eccentric or elliptical orbit.</note>, was twice at 5½° Leo [♌] or Aries [♈]: with the Sun, however, in one case at 5½° Cancer [♋], and then in the other at 5½° Capricorn [♑].

But this is not possible to occur within such a short space of time (20 or 30 years). For the periodic motions of MARS and the SUN are <term>incommensurable</term> <note>They do not return to the same relative positions in whole numbers of days or years.</note>, nor do they ever happen to fall into their quarters or opposites simultaneously after the completion of whole circuits of either, or their halves and quarters. It was necessary, therefore, to choose what was closest to the requirement, and to establish many days through these 20 years in which the Planet was observed, during which the <term>equated anomaly of commutation</term> <note>The angular distance between the Sun and the planet as seen from Earth, adjusted for orbital variations.</note> was 90° or 270°, or very nearly so, with MARS being situated in 6° Aries [♈] or Libra [♎] (or thereabouts). Afterwards, it was necessary to look through the catalog of observations of MARS for all those days to see if it had also been observed at those moments. Unless Mars had been observed very frequently by the most diligent TYCHO BRAHE, this selection was so exquisite that I could not have achieved my wish.

Since, however, TYCHO had placed the <term>apogee</term> of MARS at 23½° Leo [♌], but the position of MARS corrected through the <term>equation of the eccentric</term> <note>A mathematical correction to find a planet's true position based on its non-uniform speed.</note> was required to be 5½° Leo [♌]: therefore, the equated anomaly required was 42°. And since from his table an equation of 8° 15' 30" corresponds to the equated anomaly of 42°: therefore, a <term>mean anomaly</term> of the eccentric of 50° 16' was required; through which twelve specific times were shown to me through the twenty years from 1579 to 1600.

Whether, however, from these times there was an equated anomaly of commutation once at 90, and again at 270; or by as much as one was greater or smaller, the other was that much smaller or greater; this was investigated with skill.

One revolution of MARS has 687 days, two of the SUN have 730½: the difference in days is 43½, to which 42° 54' 23" corresponds in the <term>mean motion</term> of the SUN. By this much, therefore, the anomaly of commutation varies at the end of any revolution of Mars. When, therefore, within one biennium <note>A two-year period.</note>, two anomalies of commutation are sought that are equal to each other, with Mars being in the same position on the eccentric in both cases; it is necessary that each of those angles of commutation be 21° 27'. Within four years, 42° 54' is required; within six years, 64° 22'; within eight years, 85° 49'. And we requested, if it could be done, 90°. Therefore, it was necessary to seek our pairs of observations separated by eight years. Such a <term>pair</term> <note>original: "biga"</note> of observations was not found in the catalog of those held.

I turned, therefore, to a distance of six years, and I found at last that suitable observations existed for the year 1585 on the 18th day of May and the year 1591 on the 22nd day of January. For they corresponded to the year 1585, May 30th at 5:00 PM and 1591, January 20th at midnight <note>original: "H. 0"</note>. In both cases, the mean longitude of Mars was 6 signs 22° 43'. The TYCHONIC equation of 9° 14' 52" was to be subtracted. Therefore, Mars, by reason of the eccentric, was in 13° 28' 16" Libra [♎]. The equated <term>commutation</term> <note>The angle of "commutation" represents the apparent change in a planet's position caused by the Earth's movement around the Sun.</note> in the year 1585 was 8 signs, 4°, 23', 30'', by which it was argued, in the **PTOLEMAIC** manner, that the Planet was 64° 23' 30'' beyond the <term>perigee</term> <note>The point in an orbit closest to the center of motion.</note> of the epicycle. Likewise, the equated commutation in the year 1591 was 3 [signs], 25°, 36', 30'', by which it was argued that the Planet was 64° 23' 30'' before the perigee of the epicycle. Therefore, the angle of commutation on both sides in the diagram—**FCD** & **FCE**, or **CFI**, **CFH**—was equal. However, in the year 1585, the Sun was at 18° Gemini [♊], eighteen degrees before the <term>apogee</term> <note>The point in an orbit farthest from the center of motion.</note>; in 1591, it was at 9° Aquarius [♒], thirty-four degrees beyond the perigee. This inequality could not be avoided.

Now, as for the observations: in the year 1585, on the **18th day of May** at half an hour past midnight, Mars [♂] was seen at 0° 56' 45'' Scorpio [♏] with a northern latitude of 1° 19' 30''. **MAGINI** <note>Giovanni Antonio Magini, a contemporary astronomer and rival of Kepler.</note> reports it at 1° 5' Scorpio [♏]; he is therefore in excess by 14' 15''. Consequently, since on the evening of the 30th day at the 5th hour he reports it at 6° 48' Scorpio [♏], we will again subtract that which was erred eleven days prior; it will then retain 6° 34' Scorpio [♏]. Here we may place a few <term>scruples</term> <note>Small units of measurement, usually minutes of a degree.</note> of error because the deduction is made over twelve days, and the true daily motion might not be exactly what is applied here from **MAGINI**. For instance, on the preceding 18th of April at the 10th hour, Mars [♂] was found at 17° 37½' Libra [♎], which **MAGINI** places at 18° 0' Libra [♎]. The difference is 22½'. This difference, over the 33 days until May 18, was diminished to a measure of 14¼'. Therefore, if we proceed proportionally—since eight minutes of the difference had vanished over 33 days—in the same ratio, 3 minutes will vanish over the following 12 days. Thus, the difference on May 30 will be 11¼'. For this reason, **MARS** is more correctly placed at 6 degrees 37 minutes Scorpio [♏].

Similarly, in the year 1591, on the **22nd day of January** in the morning at the 7th hour, Mars [♂] was distant from Spica <note>The brightest star in the constellation Virgo.</note> 34° 32' 45'' [measured toward] Scorpio [♏] with a southern declination of 17° 25' at an altitude of 16°. Therefore, after accounting for horizontal variations <note>Refractions or parallaxes caused by the atmosphere and the observer's position on Earth.</note>, the declination was 17° 36'. From this, the <term>right ascension</term> <note>The celestial equivalent of longitude on Earth.</note> is 230° 23' 12'', the longitude 22° 33' Scorpio [♏], and the northern latitude 1° 6' 30''. Truly, this time is distant from ours by 1 day and 19 hours, and the daily motion according to **MAGINI** is 33''. Therefore, 59'' are owed to the intervening time. Thus, the position of Mars at January 20th at the 0 hour (the moment we said corresponded to the former) is left at 21° 34' Scorpio [♏].

## Having found two distances of the SUN from the EARTH, as well as the positions in the zodiac and the apogee of the SUN, to investigate the eccentricity of the path of the SUN (or of the EARTH according to COPERNICUS).

**H**ENCE IT IS not difficult for us to also attempt the measure of line *B C*. For let *F C* be 100,000. And because angle *D F C* is 36° 51' and *F C D* is 64° 23' 30'': therefore the remaining angle *F D C* is 78° 45' 27''. And as the sine of this angle is to *F C* 100,000, so the sine of angle *D F C* is to *D C* 61,148.

In the same way, because *E F C* is 38° 5½' minus, and *F C E* is 64° 23' 30'': *F E C* will be 77° 31' 0'' plus. Therefore *E C* is 63,186 minus.

Let the orbit of the EARTH be represented as *N E D*. In it, let *C B N* be the line of <term>apsides</term> <note>The line connecting the points of minimum and maximum distance (aphelion and perihelion) in an orbit.</note>, *N* the perihelion, *R* the <term>aphelion</term> <note>The point in an orbit furthest from the center of motion; original: "aphelium".</note>, *B* the center, *C* the point of equality of motion <note>This refers to the "equant" point, a mathematical point used to account for the observed changes in a planet's speed.</note>, and *E* and *D* the locations of two observations, which are connected with *C* and with *B*. Let *E C* be continued: and let a perpendicular *D O* descend upon it from *D*: just as from *C* and *B*, two perpendiculars descend upon *D E*, which are *C P* and *B Q*. Therefore angle *D C O* is 51° 12' 41'' and *C D O* is 38° 47' 19''. Wherefore, in units where *D C* is 61,148, *D O* will be 47,660 and *C O* 38,305. This, when added to *C E*, makes *E O* 101,491. Subtract this from *Q D*; the remainder is *P Q* 1,130½. From this, and from the known inclination of lines *E D* and *N C*, the length *C B* is easily obtained. For because *C R* is the line of <term>aphelion</term> at 5° 30' Pisces [♓]; and *C D* is at 17° 32½' Pisces [♓], because the Sun is at 17° 52' Scorpio [♏]: *D C R* will be 17° 38'. But *E D C* was 26° 3' 21''. Therefore, after subtraction, the inclination of said lines remains 8° 25' 21''. ...in the right-angled triangle, as the total sine <note>In the trigonometry of Kepler's time, the "total sine" refers to the radius of the circle, usually set at 100,000 for calculation purposes.</note> is to the tangent and secant of angle *Q P S* (8° 25' 21"), so the known *P Q* is to *Q S* (167) and *S P* (1143), which is *C B*. Therefore, the ratio of *D B* to *B C* (the ratio of the radius to the sought-to-be-found <term>eccentricity</term> <note>The distance by which the center of a planet's orbit is offset from the Sun or the Earth.</note>) is the same as 62,237 to 1143. Moreover, as 62,237 is to 100,000, so 1143 is to 1837. *This, at last, is the sought eccentricity. It would, however, be smaller if we accounted for the precession of the equinoxes, because then C E would be smaller.*

From these two observations and the assumed true position of the Sun's <term>aphelion</term> <note>The point in an orbit farthest from the Sun.</note>, the distance of our equant point *c* or *F* (which we used to think was the center) from the true center of the orbit *B*, *G*, or *M* is constructed—namely 1,837 units, where the radius of that orbit is 100,000. **TYCHO BRAHE**, however, found the eccentricity of the **SUN**—that is, the distance of the equant point *c* from the center of the **SOLAR** body *A* (in **COPERNICUS**) or the distance of the equant point of the **SOLAR** motion *a* from the center of the earth *C* (in the **TYCHONIC-PTOLEMAIC** supposition)—to be 3,584. Half of this, 1,792, differs very little indeed from 1,837. It is therefore consistent that the "halving of the eccentricity" holds true in the theory of the **SUN**, just as it had previously held true for the eccentric orbit of Mars in Chapters XIX and XX. For the observations I have used are not so precise (on account of the long deductions and the use of the controversial daily motion <note>Kepler refers to the ongoing debates regarding the exact rate of the Earth's/Sun's daily movement.</note>) that they could define anything certain to within 45 parts in a hundred thousand; to say nothing of the fact that I neglected the <term>precession</term> <note>The slow, continuous change in the orientation of an astronomical body's rotational axis.</note> of the intervening time in the eccentric motion of **MARS** and the **SUN**.

What has been demonstrated here regarding the circuit of the **EARTH** can be demonstrated in clearly the same way both for the **PTOLEMAIC** epicycle and for the **TYCHONIC** deferent <term>system</term> <note>The "deferent" is the large circular path in older astronomy upon which the smaller "epicycle" travels.</note>; provided only that the <term>apsides</term> <note>The points in an orbit closest to or farthest from the center of motion.</note> in the diagram are turned in opposite directions.

I have assumed here both that the <term>apogee</term> <note>The point in an orbit farthest from the Earth.</note> of the **SUN** was established in its correct place by **TYCHO**, and that the orbit of the **SUN** (or the **EARTH**) through which it travels bodily is arranged in a circle. Concerning which, even if the analogy to the other planets will testify to the contrary below in Chapter XLIV: the smallness of the deviation nevertheless in no way hinders our demonstration.

***

# CHAPTER XXIV.

## A more evident proof that the epicycle, or annual orb, is eccentric from the point of equality.

**T**HESE, THEREFORE, were the beginnings of this investigation—timid and laborious with so many cautions—intended so that the <term>anomaly of commutation</term> <note>A term in ancient astronomy referring to the angle used to calculate the planet's position relative to the Earth's position in its orbit.</note> would be considered equal on both sides.

<summary>Kepler concludes a trigonometric calculation to find the Earth's orbital eccentricity (1,837), noting its proximity to half of Tycho Brahe's solar eccentricity (1,792). This confirms that the Earth's orbit, like Mars's, follows the principle of "bisected eccentricity," where the center of the orbit lies halfway between the Sun and the equant point.</summary>

# PART THREE.

<margin>CHAPTER XXIV.</margin>

Now that we have once made an attempt at this matter, carried along by our daring, we shall begin to be more free in this field. For I shall search for three or any number of observed positions of **Mars**, while the Planet is always at the same point in its eccentric orbit: and from these, by the law of triangles, I shall seek as many distances of the points of the epicycle or the annual orbit from the point of equality of motion. And since a circle is described from three points, therefore from three observations of this kind I shall seek the position of the circle, and its <term>apsides</term> <note>original: "augium". These are the points in an orbit where the planet is closest to or farthest from the center of motion.</note> (which I had previously assumed by presupposition), and the <term>eccentricity</term> <note>The distance between the center of the orbit and the center of motion, such as the Sun.</note> from the point of equality. If a fourth observation is added, it will serve as a proof.

The first time shall be in the year <term>1590</term> <note>Kepler writes MDXCX, a non-standard Roman numeral for 1590.</note> March 5, old style, at 7 hours 10 minutes in the evening, because at that time **Mars** was almost without latitude <note>Meaning Mars was located exactly on the plane of the ecliptic, simplifying the geometry to two dimensions.</note>, so that no one may be hindered by any irrelevant suspicion due to its complication in perceiving the demonstration. Even though $\alpha\zeta$ is a little longer than $\alpha\eta$, which is closer to the perigee, this must be attributed to the smallness of the angles at $\zeta$, by which so small a mistake is easily made. Therefore, the circle $\delta\gamma$, which was described by COPERNICUS from point $\alpha$ (the point of uniform motion of the EARTH), is not the path of the EARTH: but it is some other circle $\vartheta\eta\zeta$ in which the EARTH revolves, whose center verges toward the same parts where the SUN is, namely at $\beta$.

In the PTOLEMAIC form, the EARTH is at A, the sphere of the SUN is $\Xi O I T$, and the putative center of the <term>epicycle</term> <note>A small circle whose center moves around the circumference of a larger one</note>—namely that around which the putative epicycle $\Delta\Gamma$ itself revolves—is equal to the theory of the Sun. It has therefore been demonstrated in the **COPERNICAN** form that the center of the **EARTH'S** circuit is in a middle position between the body of the **SUN** and the point of equality <note>The equant point, where motion appears uniform</note> of that circuit: that is, that the Earth moves unequally in its orbit; becoming slow where it recedes far from the Sun, and fast where it approaches. This is consistent with Physical reasons and the analogy of the other Planets.

In the same way, it has been demonstrated in the **PTOLEMAIC** form that the epicycle is eccentric from the point about which its motion is uniform, and that the eccentricity is half of the **SOLAR** eccentricity commonly found, and in the opposite direction.

Finally, in the **TYCHONIC** form, it has been demonstrated that the point from which the eccentricities of the Planets arise does not move on a circle concentric with the **SUN**, but is at an unequal distance throughout its circuit from the **EARTH**, about which it revolves regularly and uniformly: and indeed toward the <term>perigee</term> <note>The point in an orbit closest to the central body</note> of the **SUN**, it is farther away; toward the apogee, it is closer; again by half the eccentricity of the **SUN**. Since the Brahean system has such a great analogy with the theory of the Sun, it is likely to have an even greater one: that is, the true eccentricity of the Sun will also be only half of that which is computed from the maximum <term>equation</term> <note>The "equation" in Renaissance astronomy refers to the correction added or subtracted to the mean motion to find the true position</note>; or, what is the same thing, the Sun will utilize an <term>equant</term> <note>An imaginary point used to account for the varying speed of a planet; Kepler is arguing here that the traditional models overstate the eccentricity of the orbit itself</note>, whose eccentricity is double the eccentricity of the <term>eccentric</term> <note>The center of the circular orbit, shifted away from the central body</note>.

I confess that this argument concerning the Ptolemaic and Tychonic forms is somewhat weaker as long as we use the mean motion of the Sun with those authors. ### CHAPTER XXVI.

->Demonstration from the same observations that the epicycle from the point of attachment or axis, and the annual orbit (and thus also the path of the EARTH around the SUN, or of the SUN around the EARTH) from the center of the SOLAR or TERRESTRIAL body, is eccentric by at least half of what TYCHO BRAHE found through the equations of the SUN'S motion.<-

WE SHALL REPEAT the observations themselves carefully: On the 4th of March, in the year 1590, at 7 hours 10 minutes, Mars was found by diligent observation and calculation at 24° 22' 56'' of Aries with a latitude of 0° 3' 20'' South. At that hour, the 8th degree of Aries was setting. Therefore, Mars was quite low on the horizon. For this reason, it was being lifted <term>forward</term> <note>original: "in consequentia"—meaning moving in the direction of the zodiacal signs</note> by <term>refraction</term> <note>The bending of light as it passes through the atmosphere, which makes objects near the horizon appear higher than they are</note>, so that it is consistent that it would have appeared at 24° 20' of Aries without refraction. Its <term>parallax</term> <note>The displacement in the apparent position of an object viewed along two different lines of sight</note>, however, can only be very small, especially in longitude, for Mars was near the Sun and therefore at its greatest distance from the center of the Earth.

On the 23rd of January, in the year 1592, at 7 hours 20 minutes, based on its distance from at least one star without the testimony of another, Mars was found at 11° 32' 44'' of Aries with a latitude of 0° 1' 36'' South. Therefore, we shall change nothing on account of horizontal variations, though suspecting an uncertainty of one or two minutes.

On the 7th of December, in the year 1593, at 8 hours 0 minutes, Mars was found at 3° 6' 50'' of Aries without danger of horizontal variations, with a latitude of 7' 9'' South. However, the right ascension constructed from three stars differed by 4 minutes: the mean between the extremes was taken as the truth.

On the 25th of October, in the year 1595, at 8 hours 10 minutes, the distance of the Planet from three fixed stars was observed, and by unanimous consensus, the Planet was found at 10° 39' 25'' <insert>of Aries</insert> with a latitude of 0° 12' 41'' South.

We shall test how much <term>eccentricity</term> <note>the distance the center of an orbit is offset from the center of the system</note> is constructed from these distances. For if the theory of the SUN lacks an <term>equant</term> <note>original: æquante; a point around which a planet moves at a uniform speed</note>, the eccentricity of this circle will come out to approximately 3,600. This is because we have used the true or apparent locations of the SUN, whose point of equality must be distant from the center of the world by that much space (namely 3,600), as BRAHE <note>Tycho Brahe (1546–1601)</note> proved from Solar observations. But if a smaller eccentricity is produced, and one as close as possible to half of the Brahean value, we have won and proven that that point of equality which Brahe found is not the center of the Sun's eccentric.

You see, however (*as I may mention in passing*), at first glance, that $\alpha \zeta$ is the shortest distance, being near the <term>perigee</term> <note>the point in an orbit closest to the center</note> of the Sun; then $\alpha \epsilon$ is longer, being in Aquarius, 34 degrees from the perigee; then $\alpha \eta$, being 54 degrees from the perigee; and finally $\alpha \delta$ is the longest, because it is 80 degrees away from the perigee. And since $\alpha \zeta$ is almost at the perigee, it will therefore be slightly longer than the shortest possible distance. Likewise, since $\alpha \delta$ is near the mean longitude, it will be a little less than the average distance. Therefore, the eccentricity will come out a little greater than 1,038, which is the difference between $\delta \alpha$ and $\zeta \alpha$. And if $\delta \alpha$ takes on the dimension of 100,000, then 1,038 will be worth 1,539; and the eccentricity will turn out to be about that much, namely slightly larger. This, however, is much closer to half of the <term>TYCHONIC</term> <note>referring to Tycho Brahe's model</note> value of 1,800 than to the full 3,600.
