But it was previously stated that the eccentricity produced from $\delta$ and $\zeta$ was a little greater than 1539, assuming that $\zeta$ is very close to the perigee <note>the point in an orbit closest to the center</note>. However, since here (having admitted $\eta$ into the group in place of $\zeta$) a far greater eccentricity is produced, it is therefore suggested (though through error) that there is some point in the perigee which makes $\alpha \zeta$ even shorter. Therefore, so that this perigee could be shorter than $\alpha \zeta$, the perigee is moved to 16° Cancer (♋︎); that is, it is removed further from $\alpha \zeta$ by this line of reasoning.

But because we know in advance that the **SUN'S** perigee is not in 16° Cancer but in 6° Cancer, the cause of the slight error must be in point $\eta$, and the line $\alpha \eta$ is too long. From this, it follows that the circle $\delta, \epsilon, \eta$ would come out too large, and its radius $\delta \gamma$ too long; consequently, $\gamma \alpha$ is too long, and $\gamma$ would depart from line $\delta \eta$ in a straight line, but obliquely from point $\zeta$. Thus now the line $\gamma \alpha$ turns too much toward the following signs <note>in the order of the zodiac: Aries, Taurus, etc.</note>. Therefore, while $\delta \zeta$ remains fixed, let it be assumed that $\alpha \eta$ is shortened. Then the center $\gamma$ will approach the line $\delta \eta$ directly, and thus $\delta \gamma$ will become shorter. And because $\gamma$ approaches $\delta \eta$ perpendicularly, it therefore departs from the current $\gamma \alpha$ obliquely. Wherefore, the line drawn from $\alpha$ through the newly positioned $\gamma$ will be inclined forward toward $\delta$.

You see, therefore, that we are helped on both sides by the shortening of $\alpha \eta$. However, $\alpha \eta$ is shortened by a very slight change because of the smallness of the angles: namely, if the Planet is said to have been seen at a location slightly earlier, along a line dropped from the Sun (☉) below $\eta$. As if the observed position of Mars (♂) were 19.46 Taurus (♉︎), and the complement $\alpha \eta$ were 7.58.26, and $\eta \delta \alpha$ 5.20. 80; $\alpha \eta$ will be 67030. Therefore, the triangles are changed according to the third [position], and $\alpha \eta \delta$ becomes 23.53. 0", and $\alpha \eta \zeta$ 67.15.32". Wherefore $\delta \eta \zeta$ is 43.22.26", and $\delta \gamma \zeta$ 86.44.52". Remainder 93.15. 8". Half of $\gamma \delta \zeta$ is 46.37.44".

If anyone holds this freedom of changing the smallest details in the data as suspect—thinking that by the same freedom of changing those things that do not please us in the observations, Tycho's total eccentricity <note>Tycho Brahe's original value, which Kepler is currently challenging</note> could finally be obtained—let such a person make the attempt. When he has compared his changes with ours, let him pass judgment on which change remains within the limits of observational error <note>literally "the defect of the senses"</note>. Indeed, let him also be careful lest, emboldened by the confidence of one such procedure, he later makes a fool of himself in other matters, having found very different apogees <note>the point in an orbit furthest from the center</note> for the **SUN**.

I have certainly placed all my prejudices and leanings out in the open here, so that I fear more that I might seem troublesome to the reader than untrustworthy.

Furthermore, it should be mentioned in passing for future use that if γ δ becomes 100,000, α δ will come out as 147,443—and even greater once the things still missing are correctly accounted for.

## ON THE MOTIONS OF THE STAR MARS

Finally, so as not to be tedious, if $\alpha\vartheta$ <note>The distance from the Sun ($\alpha$) to Mars ($\vartheta$)</note> were 147,700, and the eccentric position of **MARS** in the year **1595** were in 14° 21' 7'' Taurus, and the eccentricity of the **EARTH** were 1,800, and the **EARTH'S** path were oval (as will be discussed in Chapters **XXX** and **XLIV**), the sightings would come forth as:
-> 24° 21' 13'' Aries; *Should be:* 24° 20' <-
-> 9° 23' 20'' Aries; *Should be:* 9° 24' <-

I conclude for this occasion that $\alpha\vartheta$ is approximately 147,750. 
-> 3° 2' 30'' Aries; *Should be:* 3° 4 1/2' <-
-> 19° 42' 40'' Taurus; *Should be:* 19° 42' <-

And so it has been demonstrated that $\alpha\gamma$ is approximately 1,800, whereas it ought to have been 3,600 if **TYCHO'S** findings were to be accommodated to the **COPERNICAN** form and the apparent motions of the **SUN**. Therefore, the point $\pi$—the point of the equality of the **EARTH'S** motion—must be sought on the line $\alpha\pi$ such that $\gamma\pi$ and $\gamma\alpha$ are equal. For if the **EARTH** moves uniformly around $\pi$ (that is, with the angles $\delta\pi\epsilon, \epsilon\pi\zeta, \zeta\pi\eta$ being equal), **TYCHO'S OBSERVATIONS** regarding the **SUN** will stand, and $\pi\alpha$ will be 3,600. However, with the **EARTH** being at an equal distance from point $\gamma$ at points $\delta, \epsilon, \zeta, \eta$, the **OBSERVATIONS** regarding **MARS** will also stand.

In the **PTOLEMAIC** form, a twofold drawing can be made. First, let the **EARTH** take the place of $\alpha$, the solar body; and then from $\alpha$ 
<margin>Drawing of the theory of the epicycle.</margin>
the lines of vision are cast out, parallel to $\vartheta\delta, \vartheta\epsilon, \vartheta\zeta, \vartheta\eta$. In this way, the **COPERNICAN** locations of the **EARTH** ($\delta, \epsilon, \zeta, \eta$) merge into a single **PTOLEMAIC** location for the **EARTH**. However, the star **MARS**, which according to **COPERNICUS** stood in a single point $\vartheta$, is now placed around $\vartheta$ in four locations: $\iota, \kappa, \lambda, \mu$. The description of this circle is as follows: through $\vartheta$ let a line $\vartheta\nu$ be drawn upward, parallel and equal to $\gamma\alpha$, and with center $\nu$ and a distance equal to $\gamma\epsilon$, let the circle $\iota, \kappa, \lambda, \mu$ be described. Thus, in the eccentric path which the planet's body had previously traversed according to **COPERNICUS**, it now orbits around $\vartheta$, which we can call the <term>POINT OF ATTACHMENT</term> <note>original: "punctum affixionis"</note>. 
<margin>Point of attachment. See Part One.</margin>
With the epicycle carried around in this way, the center $\nu$ will wander around $\vartheta$, sometimes inside $\vartheta\alpha$ and sometimes outside; but $\vartheta\nu$ remains always parallel to itself and to the line $\alpha\gamma$. Furthermore, the epicycle will move uniformly neither around $\vartheta$ (where it is attached) nor around the center $\nu$, but around the point $o$ above, such that $\vartheta o$ is double the distance $\vartheta\nu$. This is because in this same way, the **EARTH** also moved uniformly around $\pi$, not around the center of the orbit $\gamma$, nor around the Sun at $\alpha$.

# PART THREE.

<margin>Chapter XXVI.</margin>
These things are rightly demonstrated to flow back into the **PTOLEMAIC** epicycle <note>A small circle whose center moves around the circumference of a larger one; used in ancient astronomy to explain planetary loops.</note>. But from the epicycle into the theory of the **SUN**, they follow only by a likelihood composed from **PTOLEMAIC** tenets. *For with things standing thus, let $\alpha\tau$ be set equal to $\alpha\pi$ on the opposite parts of the same line; so that $\tau$ is the center of the equality of the **SUN'S** motion, which the **PRACTITIONERS** <note>original: "ARTIFICES"; referring to skilled astronomers or mathematical makers.</note> believed to be the center of the **SUN'S** orbit. Therefore the line $\vartheta\upsilon$ will always be parallel to the line of the **SUN'S** apogee $\alpha\tau$. If you think the diurnal parallaxes <note>The apparent shift in position of a celestial body when viewed from different points on Earth.</note> of **MARS** should be kept in that proportion to the parallaxes of the **SUN** in which they were produced by **TYCHO**; then $\iota\kappa\lambda\mu$ will also be equal to the theory of the **SUN**: because $\epsilon\vartheta o$ is equal to the eccentricity of point $\tau$, around which the **SUN** moves uniformly. But $\epsilon\vartheta$ moves in the same directions as $\iota\kappa\lambda\mu$, in which the **SUN** itself moves in its circle according to **PTOLEMY**: and at the same times, and in the same or corresponding places, both are found; the **SUN** in its eccentric, and the **PLANET** in its epicycle; so that the lines $\epsilon\tau$ through the **SUN** and $\epsilon\chi o$ through the **PLANET** are perpetually parallel, as **PTOLEMY** likewise teaches. Since all other things agree, why should this not also agree? Since $\iota\kappa\lambda\mu$ moves uniformly not around the center $\nu$ but around the upper point $o$, which has been demonstrated here by a transposition of the **EARTH'S** eccentric into the epicycle; in which for point $\alpha$ we have found $\vartheta$, for $\gamma$ we have $\upsilon$, and for $\pi$ we have $o$: so also in the **SUN** itself these parts should be divided, so that the eccentricity $\alpha\tau$, which is found from solar observations, must be bisected at $\epsilon$, and $\epsilon$ be the center of the **SUN'S** eccentric $\lambda\rho\sigma\upsilon$? For **PTOLEMY** uses such a process so that it appears that, if there were a place for the **SUN'S** appearances, it would also use entirely the same eccentricity in the **PLANET'S** epicycle as he had found in the **SUN**. Therefore, with **OBSERVATIONS** testifying to the double eccentricity of the **PTOLEMAIC** epicycle (because on account of the parallelism of lines, as said, the same triangles remain which were in the **COPERNICAN** form), the genius of **PTOLEMY** bids us also to bisect the **SUN'S** eccentricity <note>Kepler's "bisected eccentricity" means the center of the circular orbit is halfway between the Sun and the equant point (the center of uniform motion).</note>, so that the lines $\pi\iota, \rho\kappa, \sigma\lambda, \upsilon\mu$ remain parallel.*

By this reasoning, even **PTOLEMY** will be persuaded that the eccentricity $\alpha\tau$ of the **SUN'S** motion found by **TYCHO** must be bisected at $\epsilon$, so that the center of the **SUN'S** orbit is at $\epsilon$, and the equality of motion is at $\tau$.

<margin>Ptolemy's hypothesis is refuted in passing.</margin>
This argument in the **PTOLEMAIC** form (as just begun to be said) is no firmer than the **PTOLEMAIC** frame of the world itself. For because Ptolemy believes that in the three superior planets there are as many theories of epicycles, exactly equal to the theory of the **SUN** in quantity and quality, in both lines and motions of all kinds; he will not admit this one dissonance. Instead, he will gladly derive this bisection from the epicycle into the theory of the **SUN**, as if from a mirror image into the face itself.

But finally, when a comparison of hypotheses is established, it will appear that four (indeed six, as will be said elsewhere) theories of the **SUN** can descend from one theory of the **EARTH**, like many images from one substantial face: the **SUN** himself, the clearest light of truth, will melt away all this **PTOLEMAIC** apparatus like butter, and will scatter **PTOLEMY'S** followers partly into the camps of **COPERNICUS** and partly into those of **BRAHE**.

<summary>Kepler argues that the bisection of the Earth's eccentricity (the "equant") must be applied to the Sun's orbit in the Ptolemaic system to maintain consistency. He concludes by asserting that the Copernican view—where one Earth motion explains multiple solar appearances—will eventually dissolve the complex Ptolemaic machinery.</summary>

To demonstrate this, let lines be drawn from $\xi$ and $\tau$ parallel to $\alpha\beta$ itself; likewise from $\beta$ and $\chi$, let lines be drawn parallel to $\alpha\tau$, until they intersect each other: and let the intersection of the lines from $\xi$ and $\beta$ be $\phi$, from $\xi$ and $\chi$ be $\psi$, from $\tau$ and $\beta$ be $\varsigma$, and from $\tau$ and $\chi$ be $\omega$. Therefore, just as the point $\vartheta$ runs through the eccentric which, described from $\beta$, moves regularly about $\chi$: so $\nu$ runs through the eccentric which, described from $\phi$, moves regularly about $\psi$: and $o$ runs through a third eccentric, similarly equal to the former ones, which, described from $\varsigma$, moves regularly about $\omega$. Truly, the apogee <note>The point in an orbit farthest from the Earth.</note> of all three of these eccentrics is the same under the <term>Zodiac</term> <note>The belt of the heavens divided into twelve signs, used as a coordinate system.</note>, because the lines $\alpha\chi, \xi\psi, \tau\omega$ are parallel. </margin>

Someone may ask here: since the **PTOLEMAIC** epicycle <note>A small circle whose center moves along the circumference of a larger circle (the deferent).</note> has three notable points—$\nu$ the center, $\vartheta$ the point of attachment we mentioned, and $o$ the point around which its motion is uniform—and since it has been said that the line $\vartheta o$ remains parallel to $\alpha\tau$ throughout the whole circuit: what kind of circuits are then described by the remaining two points $\nu$ and $o$?

*It is indeed true that from $\alpha$, the* **Earth**, *straight lines can be projected through the centers of the two remaining eccentrics $\phi$ and $\varsigma$, which may be called the proper lines of the apogee; these will fall in the preceding parts <note>i.e., earlier in the zodiacal order</note> of the apogee $\alpha\chi$: say, $\alpha\phi$ at approximately 24° of Leo <note>original: "$\Omega$"; likely the sign for Leo</note>, and $\alpha\varsigma$ at approximately 19° of Leo. But then these lines will not pass through the proper point of equality of each eccentric. Therefore, if any of **Ptolemy's** followers does not wish to attach the epicycle to the eccentric at point $\vartheta$, but prefers to bind it at the center $\nu$, he will be forced to use two lines of apsides; one, $\alpha\phi$, of the eccentric, the other, $\alpha\psi$, of the equant <note>The mathematical point used to explain the observed speed changes of planets.</note>; and the eccentricities $\alpha\phi$ and $\alpha\psi$. How intricate and inconvenient this is (for enough was said about its absurdity in Chapter VI) let such a person judge for himself.*

*The same will occur if someone wishes to fix the epicycle to the eccentric at point $o$, around which the epicycle revolves uniformly. For then the eccentric, carrying point $o$, will have two apogees and eccentricities; one of the center in the*

AND HITHERTO the first layout has been in the **PTOLEMAIC** form. Another can be established so that the positions of the **COPERNICAN EARTH** $\delta, \epsilon, \zeta, \eta$ are granted not at $\alpha$ but at $\gamma$, such that in this diagram not $\alpha$ but $\gamma$ denotes the **EARTH** as the center of the world. In this case, the epicycle itself, and the three eccentrics of its points $\vartheta, v, o$, will be moved from their position by the small distance $\alpha \gamma$; and there will be a sheer equivalence. I shall refrain from explaining this further, lest the reader be too confused; for indeed this mention is only made for the sake of those who know a little or the curious.

IN THE **TYCHONIC** FORM, no new layout is necessary. A very brief indication suffices. The point of attachment for the eccentric is placed in four different positions at $\lambda, \rho, \sigma, v$, so that the Planet is at $\iota, \kappa, \lambda, \mu$, and the parallels $\iota \lambda, \kappa \rho, \lambda \sigma, \mu v,$ and $\vartheta \alpha$. Therefore, since **TYCHO** had said that the center of the circle of **MARS**, which he himself makes carry a double epicycle, revolves in the concentric <note>A circle sharing the same center as another.</note> of the **SUN** uniformly about $\alpha$, and did this for the sake of **PTOLEMY**; he, along with **PTOLEMY** and **COPERNICUS**, was moved by **ME** in Part One, Chapter VI, to seek that point—whether the center of the concentric or the point of attachment of the eccentric—in the very center of the **SOLAR** body itself; and this was done by physical reasons and by showing its geometric possibility. To these was added in chapters XXII and XXIII a strong argument: that unless this is done, even if observations are referred to the mean motion of the Sun, the **PTOLEMAIC** epicycle and the **BRAHEAN** deferent <note>The large circle upon which the center of an epicycle moves.</note> would become eccentric in directions precisely opposite to the eccentricity of the **SUN**. However, I promised stronger arguments, derived from **BRAHE'S** own observations, concerning the carrying of the **SUN'S** concentric, and I will produce them in the following chapters LII and LXVII. Yet it has already been proved in this chapter XXVI that this center of the concentric of **MARS** (or the point from which the eccentricity of **MARS** arises) is not found in the equal eccentric described from $\tau$, the point of equality <note>The equant point.</note> of the **SUN**, which **BRAHE** had changed along with the other authors, but in the eccentric from $\xi$, which is in the middle position between $\alpha$ and $\tau$.

Therefore, if the center of the concentric of $\mars$ <note>The symbol for Mars.</note> revolves with the **SUN**, and revolves in the eccentric described from $\xi$, then the **SUN** itself will revolve in the eccentric described from $\xi$. But its motion is regular about $\tau$. Therefore, the eccentricity of the **SUN** from $\tau$ must be bisected at $\xi$. For it is not probable, since the centers of the concentric of **MARS** and of the **SUN** revolve together, fall into apogee together, shift apogee together, are slow or fast together, and describe equal circuits, that it could happen that their circles make different departures from the **EARTH** in the same direction.

AND so far, let it suffice to have proposed this form of demonstration in the three hypotheses. In the future, whenever the same demonstration is needed, I shall use only the form of **COPERNICUS**, as it is simpler, so as not to be too long-winded. It appears, therefore, that we arrive at the same result through two other OBSERVATIONS, at $\zeta$ and $\gamma$, within the sensitivity of the senses <note>meaning within the limits of what the human eye can reliably measure</note>. For an error of a <term>sesquiscrupulus</term> <note>a "one-and-a-half scruple," or 1.5 minutes of arc</note> in observing, or in calculating the position for a day where no observation was made, can easily be committed.

BUT LET US ALSO SEE the evidence of the fifth position $\vartheta$, that is, of the observation at $\vartheta$.
We know the Sun-Earth distance $\vartheta \alpha$ is at $17^\circ 28' 33''$ Virgo ♍︎ and we set the value of $\vartheta \alpha$ at $98770$.
And the Earth-Mars line $\vartheta \eta$ was observed at $2^\circ 57' 20''$ Libra ♎︎.

And so, by a very slight shortening <note>original: "curtationem"</note> of $\alpha\eta$ itself, $\alpha\eta$ will fall plainly at the same point found in the first two observations.

THEREFORE, it appears from this that the distances $\alpha\zeta, \alpha\varepsilon, \alpha\delta, \alpha\gamma, \alpha\vartheta$, and consequently the eccentricity <note>the distance the Sun is offset from the center of the orbit</note> $\alpha\beta$, were correctly adopted and established by us. For it is impossible, if other distances were adopted, that one and the same $\alpha\eta$ and its position under the zodiac should be given from all five observations (even if they were to fit as closely as possible into a circle and were in their proper places under the zodiac).

Regarding the length <note>distance</note> of $\alpha\eta$, we shall trust most of all the observations $\zeta, \gamma, \vartheta$; for even in the common method of measuring the distances of things on EARTH, the further apart the stations are from each other, the more certainly the distance of the target is held.

But regarding its position under the zodiac, we shall trust rather the observations in $\varepsilon, \delta$ <note>two of the specific observation points in Earth's orbit</note>, because if there is any tiny error in the length of $\alpha\eta$, it is presented very obliquely to the view in $\varepsilon$ and $\delta$, and thus does not evidently change the perceived angle.

Nor should that be forgotten: that $\alpha\eta$ itself is not sensibly lengthened within the space of seven years—specifically from the year 1583 to 1590—on account of the very slow progress of the aphelion <note>the point where Mars is furthest from the Sun</note>.

SUMMARY. In the year 1590, October 31, at 6:15 in the morning, MARS, by its eccentric motion, was in 8° 19' 26'' Scorpio ♏, whereas it is placed by the hypothesis established from acronychal observations <note>observations made when Mars is directly opposite the Sun</note> in 8° 19' 29'' Scorpio ♏. Its distance was 166180, which must be lengthened on account of latitude <note>to account for the tilt of the orbit</note>, so that from it the distance of the body of MARS from the center of the SUN becomes about 166228.

# CHAPTER XXIX.
## The method for constructing the distances of the SUN and EARTH from knowledge of the eccentricity.

**I** think it has been sufficiently confirmed that the distances of the SUN and EARTH must be constructed from the halving of the eccentricity <note>Tycho Brahe had assumed the Sun's orbit had a certain eccentricity; Kepler argues here that this value must be bisected, or halved, to be physically accurate</note> found by TYCHO. Which is also clear from the summer and winter diameter of the SUN...

<summary>Kepler concludes Chapter 28 by proving that his calculated distances for Mars are consistent across five different observations from 1583 to 1590. He then begins Chapter 29, arguing that the Sun-Earth distance must be modeled using a "bisected eccentricity."</summary>
<keywords>Mars, Sun, eccentricity, Tycho Brahe, 1590 observation, Scorpio, zodiac, aphelion, acronychal, precession</keywords>

--- Page 202 ---
<meta>This page continues the transition from calculating specific observations of Mars to establishing a general geometric model for the distances in the orbits of the Earth (or Sun) and Mars. Kepler is now introducing the "bisection of the eccentricity," a key adjustment where he splits the distance between the center of uniform motion (the equant) and the physical center of the orbit, which he finds provides much more accurate results for planetary distances.</meta>

# ON THE MOTIONS OF THE STAR MARS

<margin>
CHAPTER XXIX.
</margin>

...is frequently confirmed by winter observation, as I showed in the *Optical Part of Astronomy*, chapter 11 <note>original: "Optica Astronomiæ parte"; Kepler refers to his 1604 work *Ad Vitellionem Paralipomena*</note>. But it is also wonderfully confirmed in the **COSMOGRAPHIC MYSTERY** <note>Kepler’s first book, *Mysterium Cosmographicum* (1596)</note>, chapter 15, page 53, in the table where the <term>prosthaphaereses (equations): the geometric corrections added or subtracted to a planet's mean position to find its true position</term> of **MARS, VENUS, and MERCURY** were deficient when the **LUNAR** sphere was interposed, and exceeded the truth by its omission. Now, therefore, by retaining the sphere of the **MOON**, but by bisecting the eccentricity of the **SUN**, the values will come out as close as possible to the correct ones.

And this same point will furthermore be confirmed more often and much more clearly when we see that the phenomena follow from the use of these distances resulting from the bisection (as already begun in the previous chapter). Therefore, so that these distances may be ready for our future use, I will teach how they can be easily computed, using a geometric demonstration.

In the line $\alpha\delta$, let $\alpha$ be the body of the **SUN** (*or the* **EARTH** *for* **TYCHO**, *or the center of attachment of the epicycle for* **PTOLEMY**): let $\beta$ be the center of the eccentric $\zeta\delta$ of the **EARTH** (*or of the* **SUN** *and the annual orbit for* **TYCHO**, *or of the epicycle for* **PTOLEMY**): and let $\alpha\beta$, being continued, cut the eccentric at $\delta, \varepsilon$, so that $\delta$ is the aphelion <note>the point furthest from the Sun</note> or apogee, and $\varepsilon$ is the perihelion or perigee <note>the point closest to the Sun</note>: and let $\beta\gamma$ be made equal to $\alpha\beta$: and let $\gamma$ be the center of motion or equality <note>the "equant" point</note>, at which the **EARTH** (*the center of the epicycle in* **PTOLEMY**, *the* **SUN** *and the point of attachment for all eccentrics in* **TYCHO**) describes equal angles in equal times. And let $\alpha\gamma$, from the **OBSERVATIONS OF TYCHO** and the **LANDGRAVE** <note>William IV, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel</note>, be 3600; but let $\alpha\beta$, according to my change demonstrated thus far, be 1800 <note>Kepler is "bisecting" the total eccentricity of 3600</note>. Let a perpendicular $\zeta\eta$ to $\delta\varepsilon$ be drawn through $\alpha$, cutting the circle at $\zeta, \eta$: through the same $\alpha$, let a straight line $\vartheta\iota$ be drawn at any inclination, cutting the circumference at $\vartheta, \iota$. And let the four points $\vartheta, \iota, \zeta, \eta$ be connected with the center $\beta$. Let this also be posited at the start: even if the **EARTH** (**SUN** or **PLANET**) moves uniformly around $\gamma$ and therefore non-uniformly around $\beta$, it nevertheless remains on the circumference of the circle described from $\beta$. By the equivalence demonstrated in Chapter 2 (*which, to avoid confusion, I will not apply to the general* **PTOLEMAIC** *hypothesis*), this is the same as if you said: the **EARTH** (*or the* **SUN**) *moves non-uniformly on a concentric epicycle* <note>original Greek: ὁμοκεντρεπικύκλῳ; a model where an epicycle is centered on a circle sharing the same center as the observer</note>, *with center* $\alpha$, *and a radius of the epicycle equal to* $\alpha\beta$; *and that the concentric arcs described by the center of the epicycle are similar to the arcs of the epicycle described by the* **EARTH** (*or* **SUN**), *so that both the* **EARTH** (*or* **SUN**) *and the center of the epicycle move non-uniformly in equal times, and thus they become slow together and fast together again.* I will defer the physical explanation of this hypothesis for a little while.

<margin>
Longest and shortest distance.
</margin>
**NOW**, having posited these things, I shall proceed to the work of the distances. And because $\beta\delta$ is 100,000, and $\alpha\beta\delta$ is a straight line; therefore, by the addition of both, the aphelion distance $\alpha\delta$ is obtained: and because $\beta\varepsilon$ is also 100,000; by subtracting $\alpha\beta$, the perihelion [distance] $\alpha\varepsilon$ remains.

<margin>
Distances of the middle places.
</margin>
And because $\beta\alpha\zeta$ is a right angle, and $\zeta\beta$ is 100,000, which is the <term>total sine: the radius of the circle used in calculations, often standardized to 100,000</term>; therefore $\alpha\beta$ is the sine of the angle $\alpha\zeta\beta$. Thus $\alpha\zeta\beta$ is $1^\circ 1' 53''$, namely a part of the equation <note>the correction factor</note> of the **SUN** or **EARTH**.

<summary>Kepler introduces the "bisection of eccentricity," arguing that planetary distances are more accurately modeled by splitting the distance between the equant and the Sun. He provides a geometric framework to calculate these distances using the Earth's orbit as a baseline.</summary>
<keywords>bisection of eccentricity, aphelion, perihelion, equant, Tycho Brahe, Ptolemy, prosthaphaeresis, total sine, orbit of Earth</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the geometric demonstration of how to calculate planetary distances. Kepler is moving from the general theory of bisecting the eccentricity to specific trigonometric methods for finding the distance of the planet from the Sun at any given point in its orbit.</meta>

### PART THREE.
<center>O 2</center>
<center>Possit</center>

<margin>CHAPTER XXIX.</margin>
*Optics.* For the maximum <term>equation (or prosthaphaeresis): the correction added to the mean motion to find the true position</term> of the mean longitudes, which is composed of both an Optical and a Physical part, has the total eccentricity of 3600 (or 3592) as its sine. Thus, the **SUN** or the **EARTH** moving from $\delta$ to $\zeta$ would add two days to a quarter of the periodic time; however, it would have completed the journey of only one single day beyond a quarter of the entire circuit. Thus, in this space, or quadrant of the periodic time, it would have consumed one day more than required due to Physical weakening <note>Kepler refers to his theory that the planet's motive force weakens with distance, causing it to slow down</note>.

But at the distance $\alpha\zeta$: In the right-angled triangle $\zeta\alpha\beta$, with one of the acute angles given, the other, $\zeta\beta\alpha$, will be the remainder of a right angle, namely $88^{\circ} \cdot 58' \cdot 7''$. Therefore, $\alpha\zeta$ will be the sine of this angle, specifically 99884; and $\alpha\eta$ opposite to it is the same.

<margin>The remaining distances.</margin>
To find the intermediate distances for two opposite degrees of the equated anomaly, let $\vartheta$ be observed, passing through the body $a$ <note>Kepler likely means $\alpha$, the Sun</note> from which the eccentricity is computed. *For $\delta\vartheta$ and $\varepsilon\iota$ are equated and opposite anomalies, since $a$ is placed between them on the same straight line.* Let a perpendicular $\beta\kappa$ fall from $\beta$ onto $\vartheta\iota$, such that $\vartheta\kappa$ and $\kappa\iota$ are equal. Therefore, in the right-angled triangle $\beta\kappa\alpha$, the base $\beta\alpha$ is given, as is the angle $\kappa\alpha\beta$ from the number of whole degrees of the <term>equated anomaly: the angle of the planet as seen from the Sun</term> that was chosen, and its complement to a quadrant, $\kappa\beta\alpha$. Thus, the sides $\kappa\alpha$ and $\kappa\beta$ will not be unknown. Furthermore, $\kappa\beta$ is the sine of the angle $\kappa\vartheta\beta$ or $\kappa\iota\beta$; once this is given, its complement to a semicircle, $\beta\vartheta$ or $\iota\beta$, and its sine, namely the line $\vartheta\kappa$ or $\kappa\iota$, will also be known. Therefore, by adding $\kappa\alpha$ to $\kappa\vartheta$, $\alpha\vartheta$ is obtained; by subtracting the same from $\kappa\iota$, $\alpha\iota$ is obtained. The former distance belongs to the equated anomaly $\delta\alpha\vartheta$, and the latter to the equated anomaly $\delta\alpha\iota$, which also has an equal value in the first semicircle; so that the former is as far from the <term>aphelion: the point in orbit farthest from the Sun</term> in the semicircle $\delta\vartheta$ as the latter is in the semicircle $\delta\eta$.

<margin>A shortcut.</margin>
Now let the line $\mu\nu$ be drawn through $\alpha$, cutting the circle at $\mu$ and $\nu$, and making the angle $\mu\alpha\delta$ equal to the angle $\kappa\beta\alpha$. Let the perpendicular $\beta\lambda$ descend from $\beta$ onto $\mu\nu$, bisecting $\mu\nu$ at $\lambda$, and let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be connected with $\beta$. Since $\kappa\alpha\beta$ is an angle of whole degrees, the remainder $\kappa\beta\alpha$ will also be so, and $\mu\alpha\delta$ (being equal to it) will be of whole degrees. In the similar triangles $\beta\kappa\alpha$ and $\beta\lambda\alpha$, side $\kappa\alpha$ will be equal to side $\lambda\beta$, and $\kappa\beta$ to $\lambda\alpha$. Now, $\lambda\beta$ is the sine of the angle $\lambda\mu\beta$ and $\lambda\nu\beta$; the complement of $\lambda\mu\beta$ is $\lambda\beta\mu$ and $\lambda\beta\nu$, and its sine is the line $\lambda\mu$ and $\lambda\nu$; and the difference between $\alpha\mu$ and $\alpha\nu$ is $\lambda\alpha$. But the quantities $\lambda\alpha$ and $\lambda\beta$ have already been found in triangle $\alpha\beta\kappa$. Therefore, with the help of one triangle, four distances can be found at equal angles to $\alpha$, removed from the line of apsides and its perpendicular $\zeta\eta$ drawn through $a$; for $\mu\alpha\zeta$ is equal to $\vartheta\alpha\delta$, and $\nu\alpha\eta$ is equal to $\iota\alpha\varepsilon$.

<margin>Where the mean distance is between the longest and shortest.</margin>
Thus, the longest distance is at $\delta$, the shortest at $\varepsilon$. But the mean distance, equal to $\beta\zeta$ <note>The radius of the circle</note>, is not at $\zeta\eta$; nor is it on the line through $\beta$ parallel to $\zeta\alpha$, which we may call $\xi o$. For $\alpha\zeta$ is smaller than $\beta\zeta$, because it is subtended by the smaller angle $\zeta\beta\alpha$ rather than $\zeta\alpha\beta$ (which is a right angle); and the line $\alpha\xi$ is longer than $\beta\xi$, because it is subtended by the larger angle $\xi\beta\alpha$ (being a right angle), while $\xi\beta$ is subtended by the smaller angle $\xi\alpha\beta$.

In order to geometrically designate the location of the mean distance, let $\alpha\beta$ be bisected at point $\sigma$, and through this point let $\pi\rho$ be drawn perpendicular to $\alpha\beta$, cutting the circle at $\pi$ and $\rho$. I say that these are the points equidistant from $\alpha$ and $\beta$.

For let either of the points, $\pi$, be connected with $\alpha$ and with $\beta$. Then $\pi\alpha$ and $\pi\beta$ will be subtended by equal (specifically, right) angles $\pi\sigma\alpha$ and $\pi\sigma\beta$, and $\alpha\sigma$ and $\sigma\beta$ are equal, and $\pi\sigma$ is shared. Therefore, $\pi\alpha$ and $\pi\beta$ are equal. And so the demonstration used by **REINHOLD** <note>Erasmus Reinhold (1511–1553), an astronomer who published the Prutenic Tables</note> concerning the whole line $\alpha\gamma$ and its midpoint $\beta$ remains true for the point $\sigma$ and the half-line $\alpha\beta$.

<summary>Kepler provides a geometric method for calculating the planet's distance from the Sun at various points in its orbit. He proves that the "mean distance" (the radius of the orbit) occurs at a point determined by bisecting the eccentricity.</summary>
<keywords>eccentricity, equated anomaly, mean distance, aphelion, Reinhold, geometry, trigonometry, orbit of Mars</keywords>

<page-num>160</page-num>
# ON THE MOTIONS OF THE STAR MARS

<margin>
Where is the maximum equation?

CHAPTER XXIX.
</margin>

Someone might therefore think that at point $\pi$, since the distance $\alpha\pi$ becomes equal to the radius $\beta\pi$, the angle $\beta\pi\alpha$ would also be greater than the angle $\beta\zeta\alpha$, and thus the maximum <term>equation: the correction used to find a planet's true position from its average position</term> would occur at $\pi$. *This uses the argument that the line $\beta\alpha$ is presented more directly to $\pi$ than to $\zeta$. Yet what was proposed is not true. For however much more obliquely $\beta\alpha$ regards $\zeta$, $\pi$ is in turn further away than $\zeta$; since $\pi\sigma$ becomes longer than $\zeta\alpha$. For $\pi\beta\sigma$ is greater than $\zeta\beta\alpha$, which $\zeta\alpha$ subtends.*

Therefore, PTOLEMY <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century astronomer</note> demonstrated correctly, and after him REINHOLD in the *Theoricae* <note>Erasmus Reinhold, who published influential commentaries on planetary theory in the 16th century</note>, that the maximum equation (specifically the solitary or "Optical" equation of the <term>eccentric: a circular orbit where the center of motion is not the center of the Earth/Sun</term>) occurs at $\zeta$. However, I shall present that demonstration here in another, easier form. Let there be any point above $\zeta$, such as $\vartheta$, and any point below $\eta$ or $\zeta$, such as $\iota$. Let these be connected with $\alpha$, and from $\beta$ let perpendiculars $\beta\chi$ fall upon the lines $\vartheta\alpha$ or $\iota\alpha$ (extended). Since the angles $\delta\alpha\zeta$ and $\beta\chi\alpha$ are equal (being right angles), and $\chi\beta\alpha$ and $\chi\alpha\beta$ joined together equal one right angle; then, by taking away the equal angles $\delta\alpha\vartheta$ or $\beta\alpha\chi$, the remaining angles $\vartheta\alpha\zeta$ and $\chi\beta\alpha$ are equal. And first, since some line is drawn through $\alpha$ above point $\zeta$, such as $\vartheta\alpha$, whether $\vartheta$ is near to or far from $\zeta$, the perpendicular $\beta\chi$ simultaneously declines from $\beta\alpha$. Moreover, $\beta\alpha$ is greater than any of the perpendiculars $\beta\chi$, since $\beta\alpha$ subtends the right angle $\beta\chi\alpha$, while $\beta\chi$ subtends the acute and smaller angle $\beta\alpha\chi$. Since, however, $\beta\zeta, \beta\vartheta, \beta\iota$ are equal, and $\beta\alpha\zeta, \beta\chi\vartheta, \beta\chi\iota$ are right angles, they all fall within the same semicircle, the diameter of which is equal to $\beta\zeta, \beta\vartheta, \beta\iota$. Thus $\beta\alpha$ (being longer) subtends a greater circumference of such a semicircle than $\beta\chi$ or any of the perpendiculars; and accordingly, its angle $\beta\zeta\alpha$ will be greater than $\beta\vartheta\alpha$, or the angle of <term>prosthaphaeresis: a synonym for the "equation" or correction added to the mean motion</term> of any other point above $\zeta$, such as $\pi$ or $\epsilon$. Which was to be demonstrated.

What has been said in this chapter about computing the distances of the **SUN** and the **EARTH** will also hold true for **MARS**, so long as it is assumed that the orbits of the planets are perfect circles. Once this is discovered to be false <note>This is a crucial hint: Kepler is leading the reader toward his discovery of elliptical orbits</note>, another **METHOD** for computing them will be handed down.

---

### CHAPTER XXX.

## Table of the distance of the SUN from the EARTH and its use.

Having constructed the distances of the **SUN** in this manner for the whole degrees of the equated anomaly of the entire semicircle (for those in the other semicircle, being equally distant from the <term>apogee: the point in the orbit furthest from the Sun/Earth</term>, are also equal to these), we have gathered them here into a small table, which has three columns. In the first column, which we called the mean anomaly, are the angles $\delta\vartheta\mu, \delta\vartheta\xi, \delta\vartheta\epsilon, \delta\vartheta\iota, \delta\vartheta\nu$ composed of the angles $\delta\alpha\mu, \delta\alpha\vartheta, \delta\alpha\xi, \delta\alpha\nu$ of whole degrees, and from their Optical or eccentric equations, such as $\beta\mu\alpha, \beta\vartheta\alpha, \beta\xi\alpha, \beta\iota\alpha, \beta\nu\alpha$. In the second column, the distances themselves $\alpha\mu, \alpha\vartheta, \alpha\xi, \alpha\iota, \alpha\nu$ are placed alongside. In the third, under the title of equated anomaly...

<page-num>161</page-num>

# PART THREE.

<sig>O 3</sig>

<note>original catchword: Anoma-</note>

The angles not depicted here are positioned according to a logic that will be revealed partly now and partly in Chapters 31 and 40. They are produced by subtracting the optical <term>equations: the geometric corrections used to account for the difference between a planet's uniform motion and its observed position</term> <note>original: "αμβ & c."</note> from the total angles <note>original: "δαμ & c."</note>. Therefore, we have not given a specific column for these integrated angles <note>original: "δαμ"</note> of whole degrees; because they are the arithmetic mean between the angles in the side columns, they are easily understood by themselves and are not used, as we shall hear.

<margin>
Instruction on using the table.
</margin>

By entering, therefore, with either the <term>mean anomaly: the position of a planet assuming it moves at a constant speed in a circle</term> or the <term>equated anomaly: the position of a planet after correcting for its eccentric orbit</term>, as use requires, and seeking either one in its own column (or using its complement to the full circle if it exceeds a semicircle), you will find the required distance from the EARTH, in units where the radius of the orbit is 100,000 and the <term>eccentricity: the distance the sun is offset from the center of the orbit</term> is 1,800.

<margin>
The path of the Sun or Earth through this table is assumed to be an oval.
</margin>

It is true that by this method (while we assign the distance from point *zeta* <note>original: "ζ"</note> of the angle *delta-alpha-zeta* <note>original: "δαζ"</note> to an angle that is smaller than the angle *delta-alpha-zeta* by the same amount that *delta-alpha-zeta* is smaller than *delta-beta-zeta*), the path of the EARTH (or the SUN) around point *alpha* <note>the Sun</note> is fashioned not as a perfectly circular path, but as an **oval**. For because (for example) the distance *alpha-xi* <note>original: "αξ"</note> was constructed through a full angle *delta-alpha-xi* <note>original: "δαξ"</note> of 90°, and it was established in the operation that this angle *delta-alpha-xi* was the equated anomaly; yet now you are ordered to extract the distances through the angles of anomaly (which in our table is called "equated") diminished by the <term>equation: or "prosthaphæresis," the adjustment for the observer's position</term> *beta-alpha-xi* <note>original: "βαξ"</note>. 

Therefore, it happens that for 90° you do not extract 99,984, even though you previously constructed 99,984 for 90°. For here, in the region of 99,984, you find an equated anomaly of 88° 58' 7", which is not yours. For 90° was proposed to you, which, when sought further down, shows 99,953, whereas by the law of a circle, the distance *alpha-xi* or *alpha-nu* <note>original: "αν"</note> ought to have been 99,984. Thus, all distances are reduced at the sides, mostly around the points *delta* and *epsilon* <note>original: "δ.ε."</note>, but not at all at the points themselves. In this way, an explicitly **oval** path is substituted for a circular one. 

The same thing will happen to you if you enter via the mean anomaly provided to you from elsewhere. For the mean anomaly noted above, when the diagram was described, the angles were at *gamma* <note>original: "γ"</note>. Now, however, you enter the angles at *beta* <note>original: "β"</note>, which are smaller than those at *gamma* by the optical equation. And a mean anomaly of 91° 1' 55" shows you 99,984. Above, indeed, the angle *delta-beta-zeta* <note>original: "δβζ"</note> was that large; yet that was not the mean anomaly there, for the mean anomaly *delta-gamma-zeta* <note>original: "δγζ"</note> had been even larger. Thus, that mean anomaly of 91° 1' 53" had constructed a longer distance there than the mean anomaly of the same magnitude (91° 1' 53") shows here. 

I say that ALL this IS TRUE. But there is no reason why you should allow yourself to be hindered. Indeed, because we are dealing with a difference of one degree, you see that the distances within one degree do not vary by more than 31 parts out of a hundred thousand. Thus, nothing sensible would be erred, even if this were done backwards. You will find the cause of this matter—the analogy of the other planets to be brought into the theory of the SUN—below in Chapter 44 and following. It is therefore not done backwards, but most correctly, as far as it concerns the quality of the figure that the Planet is supposed to describe.

But as far as the quantity is concerned, the "medicine" <note>Kepler's playful term for his mathematical correction</note> exceeds the limit. For the equated anomaly of 88° 58' 7", to which the mean anomaly of 91° 1' 53" responds, ought not to have shown 99,984, but 100,000, which is the midpoint between the distances of the diagram and the table. The cause of this assertion must be deferred to Chapter 55 and those following.

However, it has already been said that we will wander by nothing sensible if we err by 31 parts. Much less, therefore, will it harm us perceptibly if we err by only half, namely 16 parts. Therefore, in the meantime, we safely admit this tiny error, so that we may accommodate ourselves to the understanding of the reader who has progressed this far in reading, and so that we do not seem to presuppose that which was to be demonstrated.

<summary>Kepler explains how to use his table of planetary distances and admits that his calculations imply the Earth's orbit is an oval rather than a circle. He argues that the resulting mathematical errors are too small to be noticed by observers at this stage, deferring the physical proof of non-circular orbits to later chapters.</summary>

### CHAPTER XXXI.

# That the equations of the SUN set forth by TYCHO are not sensibly disturbed by the bisection of the SUN’S eccentricity: and on the four ways of computing them.

<margin>
In the following chapters, confusion will arise for the unwary reader. The motion of the Sun (according to Brahe), or the Earth (according to Copernicus), or the epicycle (according to Ptolemy), which is the cause of the SECOND inequality <note>The apparent backward motion or "retrograde" loops of planets</note> for the other planets, itself also participates in the FIRST inequality <note>The variation in speed due to the elliptical or eccentric shape of the orbit</note>.
</margin>

**BUT** <note>original: "SED," beginning with a decorative initial</note> lest any suspicion stand in our way as we proceed to what follows, we shall explore in the customary and PTOLEMAIC form of the first inequality whether any diversity in the equations occurs in the CASE OF THE SUN now that the eccentricity has been bisected <note>The "bisection of eccentricity" refers to Kepler's discovery that the center of a planet's circular orbit lies halfway between the Sun and the "equant point" (the center of uniform motion)</note>.

Let the total eccentricity first be 3600 on the line of apsides <note>The line connecting the closest and furthest points of an orbit</note> AF, and therefore let CE and CD be the radii of the ORB: and let the anomaly <note>The angle measuring a planet's progress from its furthest point</note> FAE be 45°, and FAD be 135°. It is clear that however great the discrepancy may be, it will be greatest around these anomaly points. For at the mean longitudes <note>Positions at 90° and 270°</note>, the equations come out exactly the same, since the value 3600 sought in both sines and tangents yields the same arc.

Therefore, as the radius CE is to the sine of angle CAE or CAD, so is the eccentricity CA to the equation <note>The correction applied to the mean motion to find the true position</note> CEA or CDA, which is 1° 27’ 31” on both sides. And in this first way PTOLEMY computed the equations of the SUN, and from PTOLEMY, COPERNICUS, and from them BRAHE; each used an eccentricity AC as great as he found from his own observations.

Now follows the second way of computing these same equations, which PTOLEMY used for the other PLANETS, and which I must use, since I have demonstrated in this third part that the center of the eccentric is not at point C (the point of uniform motion), but at point B, halfway between A (the center of the world) and C (the point of uniformity).

Therefore, let CA be bisected at B, and let EB and BC <note>likely BD intended</note> be the radius of the ORB; by the same METHOD, the part of the equation BEA and BDA will be 0° 43’ 46”. This, when added to EAB and DAB, will constitute EBC as 45° 43’ 46” and DBC as 135° 43’ 46”. Therefore, from the sides and the included angle, BEC results in 43’ 38” and BDC in 43’ 42”, and thus the total CEA is 1° 27’ 24” and CDA is 1° 27’ 28”, exactly the same as the previous result. Thus, in the appendix to TYCHO BRAHE’S *Progymnasmata* on page 821, where the difference between the two calculations is given as 1 1/6, read instead 6 1/6. And this is according to the doctrine of Chapter IV from the form of the vicarious hypothesis <note>A mathematical model Kepler used as an intermediary step before finding the elliptical laws</note>.

And since you see how nearly equal the parts of the equation are in this PTOLEMAIC form of a particular hypothesis (for the Optical part was 43’ 46”, the Physical part at E was 43’ 38”, and at D was 43’ 42”): from this the reason is clear to you why in the preceding chapter, in the construction of the TABLE, I did nothing other than double the prosthaphaeresis <note>original: "prosthaphæreſin," the Greek term for the equation or correction angle</note> to constitute the total prosthaphaeresis. This is the third way of computing the prosthaphaereses of the SUN. For at the apogee and perigee <note>The furthest and closest points to the center of motion</note>, both parts of the equation vanish; at the mean longitudes, the parts are again equal, as was just said. Therefore, since these three methods of computing the equations coincide plainly at eight points arranged around the whole circle, they will coincide for all practical purposes everywhere. This is due to the smallness of the eccentricity. If it were larger, these things certainly would not hold true in all respects.

Now <note>catchword: Nunc</note>

<summary>Kepler demonstrates that bisecting the eccentricity of the Sun's orbit—moving the center of the circle—does not significantly change the observational results recorded by Tycho Brahe. This allows him to reconcile his new physical theories with established astronomical data.</summary>

Now I shall prepare myself over the next eight chapters for the fourth way of computing the equation—calculating it not through a fictitious hypothesis but from the very nature of things—so that this fourth way can finally follow in the fortieth chapter.

# CHAPTER XXXII.

## The power that moves the Planet in a circle weakens as it departs from its source.

I STATED ABOVE <note>original: "DIXI SVPRA," beginning with a decorative initial</note> that Ptolemy, taught by observations, bisected the eccentricities <note>Split the distance between the center of the world and the center of uniform motion</note> of the three superior planets <note>Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn</note>, and that Copernicus imitated him; Tycho Brahe’s observations of MARS also urge the same, as appeared in chapters 19 and 20, and will appear much more certainly below in chapter 42. Furthermore, Tycho followed this as closely as possible in the case of the MOON. Now the same has also been demonstrated in the theory of the SUN (according to Tycho) or the EARTH (according to Copernicus). Indeed, nothing prevents us from believing the same of VENUS and MERCURY. In fact, I have already demonstrated that the opinion arose from this that the centers of the eccentrics <note>The center points of the planets' circular paths</note> of these planets travel in a small annual circle. Therefore, all Planets have this.
<margin>* there are now more <note>Kepler likely refers to the years since the 1596 publication of his first book</note></margin>
Since, therefore, in my *COSMOGRAPHIC MYSTERY* <note>original: *Mysterium Cosmographicum*</note> published *eight years ago, I deferred this dispute regarding the cause of the PTOLEMAIC equant <note>An imaginary point used to explain why planets seem to speed up and slow down</note> for this reason alone: that it could not be said from common Astronomy whether the SUN or EARTH also used an equant point and a bisection of its eccentricity; it is indeed fitting now that the matter be clear. We now have it confirmed by the testimony of a purer Astronomy that an equant is altogether present in the theory of the SUN or EARTH. This having been demonstrated, I say, it is fitting that the cause of the PTOLEMAIC equant assigned by me in the *COSMOGRAPHIC MYSTERY* be held as just and legitimate, since it is universal and common to all Planets. I shall therefore explain it more fully in this part of the work.

And because the explanation will be general, I shall use the word PLANET. Let the reader, however, in this and the next few chapters always understand specifically the EARTH (in the system of Copernicus) or the SUN (in the system of Tycho).

First, let him know that in every PTOLEMAIC hypothesis constructed in this form, however great the eccentricity may be, the speed in perihelion <note>the point closest to the sun</note> and the slowness in aphelion <note>the point furthest from the sun</note> are proportional, as closely as possible, to the lines drawn from the center of the world to the PLANET.

*In the diagram of chapter 29, in which α was the center of the world, and β the center of the eccentric δ ε, and γ the equant point, let a circle representing the equant υ φ be drawn with center γ and distance β δ. And through α the center of the world, from which the eccentricity is computed (which in the present business is the SUN for Copernicus and the EARTH for others), let the straight line ψ ω be drawn, cutting the eccentric at ψ and ω, so that the Planet is at ψ and ω, arcs of the eccentric*

<margin>CHAPTER XXXII.</margin>

[Let us consider] the arcs of the eccentric $\delta$ $\psi$ and $\epsilon$ $\omega$ that have been completed, the former starting from the aphelion <note>The point in an orbit furthest from the Sun; original: "aphelio"</note> or apogee, the latter from the perihelion <note>The point in an orbit closest to the Sun; original: "perihelio"</note> or perigee. These arcs are assumed to appear equal when viewed from point $a$ <note>Kepler places the observer/Sun at point $a$</note>, because the line $\gamma$ $\omega$ makes the vertical angles <note>original: "ad verticem"</note> $\psi$ $a$ $\delta$ and $\omega$ $a$ $\epsilon$ equal. However, since the arcs $\delta$ $\psi$ and $\epsilon$ $\omega$ are assumed to be very small, specifically at the apsides <note>The highest and lowest points of the orbit</note> $\delta$ and $\epsilon$, they do not differ perceptibly from straight lines. Therefore, just as if $\delta$ $\psi$ and $\epsilon$ $\omega$ were rectilinear triangles, and $\delta, \epsilon$ were right angles, and $a$ were the common vertex, the ratio of $\delta a$ to $\epsilon a$ will be the same as the ratio of the arc $\delta \psi$ to the arc $\epsilon \omega$. But the distance $a \delta$ is longer than $a \epsilon$: therefore the arc $\delta \psi$ is also longer than $\epsilon \omega$. These arcs, though truly unequal in length, appear equal when seen from $a$.

The question now is: how much time does the Planet spend in each arc according to the doctrine and hypothesis of <term>PTOLEMY</term> <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century astronomer whose Earth-centered model Kepler is here refining</note>, when he employs an equant <note>A mathematical tool used by ancient astronomers to account for the observed changes in a planet's speed</note>? Therefore, let lines be drawn from the center $\gamma$ through the markers $\psi$ and $\omega$, intersecting the equant circle at $\chi$ and $\tau$. <term>PTOLEMY</term> will then say: since the whole circle of the equant $\upsilon \phi$ represents the periodic time of the <term>PLANET</term>, then the arc $\upsilon \chi$ is the measure of time that the <term>PLANET</term> spends in the arc of the eccentric $\delta \psi$, and $\phi \tau$ is the measure of the time that the <term>PLANET</term> spends in the arc of the eccentric $\epsilon \omega$.

But I argue that the arc of time $\upsilon \chi$ delineated in this way, as <term>PTOLEMY</term> intended, is to the arc of the path $\delta \psi$ very nearly as the distance $a \delta$ (of the arc $\delta \psi$ from the center of the world) is to the mean distance $\beta \delta$ of the points $\pi, \rho$ from $a$. Similarly, the arc of time $\phi \tau$ is to the arc of the path $\epsilon \omega$ very nearly as the distance $a \epsilon$ (of the arc $\epsilon \omega$ from the center of the world $a$) is to the mean distance $\epsilon \beta$ and $a \pi$ from the center of the world, which can occur at the markers $\pi, \rho$. For, as before, just as $\gamma \upsilon$ is to $\gamma \delta$, so $\upsilon \chi$ is to $\delta \psi$; and as $\gamma \phi$ is to $\gamma \epsilon$, so $\phi \tau$ is to $\epsilon \omega$. But $\gamma \upsilon$ is to $\gamma \delta$ almost as $\beta \delta$ (or $\gamma \upsilon$) is to $a \delta$. This is evident because $\beta \delta$ is the arithmetic mean <note>The average of two values</note> between $\gamma \delta$ and $a \delta$. For <term>PTOLEMY</term> makes the distances $a \beta$ and $\beta \gamma$ equal. The arithmetic mean between two terms, when the ratio between them is small, is only imperceptibly greater than the geometric mean. For example, between 10 and 12, the arithmetic mean is 11, while the geometric mean is approximately $10 \frac{19}{20}$. The difference between the two means is less than one-twentieth of one part. And yet these numbers are typical for the theory of <term>MARS</term>, which has the largest eccentricity <note>How much the orbit deviates from a perfect circle</note> of all the planets in <term>PTOLEMY</term>'s work.

Since, therefore, the ratio of $\gamma \upsilon$ to $\gamma \delta$ is imperceptibly greater than the ratio of $a \delta$ to $\delta \beta$, the ratio of $\chi \upsilon$ to $\psi \delta$ will also be imperceptibly greater than the ratio of $a \delta$ to $\delta \beta$. Similarly, as $\gamma \epsilon$ is to $\gamma \phi$, so $\epsilon \omega$ is to $\phi \tau$. But $\gamma \epsilon$ to $\gamma \phi$ is almost as $\epsilon \beta$ to $a \epsilon$; indeed, that first ratio is imperceptibly less than the second. Therefore, the ratio of $\epsilon \omega$ to $\phi \tau$ is also imperceptibly less than the ratio of $\epsilon \beta$ to $a \epsilon$.

Now let us permute these. For the ratio of $a \delta$ to $\delta \beta$ is imperceptibly less than the ratio of $\delta \psi$ (or $\beta \epsilon$) to $\epsilon a$: because $\beta \delta$ (or $\beta \epsilon$) is the arithmetic mean between $a \delta$ and $a \epsilon$, as stated before. It has been proved, however, that the ratio of $\upsilon \chi$ to $\delta \psi$ is greater than the ratio of $a \delta$ to $\delta \beta$, from the two smaller [ratios]: and the ratio of $\epsilon \omega$ to $\phi \tau$ is less than the ratio—

<margin>CHAPTER XXXII.</margin>
...by the proportion of $\epsilon\beta$ to $a\epsilon$, the greater of the two: so that just as with the two $a\delta$ to $\delta\beta$, and $\epsilon\beta$ to $a\epsilon$, the former is smaller and the latter larger; so too with the two $\upsilon\chi$ to $\delta\psi$, and $\epsilon\omega$ to $\phi\tau$, the former is larger and the latter smaller. Therefore, there is even a certain compensation for that imperceptible difference, so that it is much closer to the truth that the proportion of $\upsilon\chi$ to $\delta\psi$ is exactly <note>original: "ad unguem", literally "to the fingernail," meaning perfectly or precisely</note> equal to the proportion of $\epsilon\omega$ to $\phi\tau$.

Therefore, if the arcs $\delta\psi$ and $\epsilon\omega$ are taken as equal (which until now were unequal), each will be a mean proportional between $\upsilon\chi$, the delay <note>original: "mora", the time spent traversing a specific arc</note> at the **aphelion**, and $\phi\tau$, the delay at the **perihelion**. And thus the proportion of $\upsilon\chi$ to $\phi\tau$ (with $\delta\psi$ and $\epsilon\omega$ being equal) will be double the proportion of $a\delta$ to $d\beta$ or $\beta e$ to $\epsilon a$—the former being smaller, the latter larger by some imperceptible amount. And since the proportion of $a\delta$ to $a\epsilon$ is also double either of these (for it is composed of both, which are nearly equal, the arithmetic mean $d\beta$ or $\beta\epsilon$ being the middle example): therefore, when the arcs of the eccentric $\delta\psi$ and $\epsilon\omega$ are equal, the proportion of the delay $\upsilon\chi$ to the delay $\phi\tau$ will be equal to the proportion of the distance $a\delta$ to $a\epsilon$. To put it more clearly: by as much as distance $a\delta$ is longer than $a\epsilon$, by that much longer does the **PLANET** remain in any certain arc of the eccentric at $\delta$ than in an equal arc of the eccentric at $\epsilon$. And this follows from the arrangement of the <margin>* Understand this as the specific form serving the first inequality.</margin> * **PTOLEMAIC** model and its **equant point** <note>The mathematical point used in ancient astronomy to account for the observed changes in speed of the planets</note> by a certain and legitimate demonstration, as far as the locations near the **apogee** and **perigee** are concerned. In other cases, a very slight difference appears, and the more evident it is in the demonstration, the smaller it is in effect: because, for example, the proportion of $a\mu$ to $a\nu$ is smaller, and $a\vartheta$ to $a\iota$ much smaller, than the ratio of $a\delta$ to $a\epsilon$, which is the greatest of all and of the greatest effect.

***

# C H A P T E R  X X X I I I .

## That the power which moves the Planets resides in the body of the S U N .

Since it was demonstrated in the previous chapter that the delays of a **PLANET** in equal parts of the eccentric circle (or in equal spaces of the ethereal air) are in the same proportion as the distances <note>original: "abscessus"</note> of those same spaces from the point from which the eccentricity is calculated: or more simply; the further the **PLANET** is from that point which is assumed to be the center of the world, the more weakly it is driven around 그 point: it is therefore necessary that the cause of this weakening exists either in the body of the **PLANET** itself and its inherent moving force, or in the assumed center of the world itself.

Indeed, it is a very common axiom throughout all natural Philosophy: that of those things which occur at the same time and in the same way, and take on the same dimensions everywhere, one is either the cause of the other, or both are effects of the same cause. As in this case, the strengthening and weakening of the motion perpetually coincides, in proportion, with the approach to and recession from the center of the world. Therefore, either that weakening will be the cause of the star's departure from the center of the world, or the departure the cause of the weakening, or there will be some common cause for both. But neither...

<meta>The catchword at the bottom of the page is "neque" (neither), which will begin the argument on the next page that the cause is not in the planet's own soul or force alone.</meta>

<summary>Kepler mathematically concludes that a planet's orbital speed is inversely proportional to its distance from the Sun. He then begins a physical argument, asserting that this relationship implies the Sun is the physical source of the force moving the planets.</summary>

<keywords>aphelion, perihelion, distance-speed law, equant point, Ptolemaic model, celestial physics, moving power, Sun, eccentricity</keywords>

<meta>This page transitions from the geometric demonstrations of Chapter 32 to the physical arguments of Chapter 33. Kepler is moving from mathematical models to "celestial physics," arguing that the cause of planetary motion must reside in the Sun.</meta>

<page-num>168</page-num>
<header>ON THE MOTIONS OF THE STAR MARS</header>

<margin>CHAPTER XXXIII.</margin>...nor can anyone suppose that some third thing concurs, which might be a common cause for these two; and in the following chapters it will become clear that it is not necessary for us to devise any such thing, since those two are sufficient for themselves.

Furthermore, it is not consistent with nature that the strength or weakness in the **motion in longitude** <note>the movement of a planet along its orbital path</note> should be the cause of its distance from the center. For distance from the center is prior in thought and nature to the motion in longitude. Indeed, motion in longitude never occurs without a distance from the center, since it requires space in which to be completed; distance from the center, however, can be imagined without motion. Therefore, distance will be the cause of the vigor in the motion, and a greater or lesser distance will cause a greater or lesser **delay** <note>original: "moræ", referring to the time spent traversing a portion of the orbit</note>.

And since distance is of the class of "relations," the existence of which falls back upon its endpoints—and since a relation of itself (without respect to its endpoints) can have no efficiency—it follows, therefore, as has been said, that the cause of the varying vigor in the motion resides in one or the other of the endpoints.

The body of the **PLANET** itself, however, is made neither heavier by departure nor lighter by approach.

As for an **animal force** <note>original: "animalem vim", the 17th-century idea that planets were moved by a soul or indwelling intelligence</note> that would provide motion to the star, residing in the mobile body of the **PLANET**, it would perhaps be absurd to say that it is intensified and relaxed so many times without exhaustion or old age. Add to this that it cannot be understood how this animal force would transport its own body through the spaces of the world, since there are no solid spheres <note>crystalline or physical shells to which planets were once thought to be attached</note>, as *Tycho Brahe* has demonstrated. Nor are there the aids of wings or feet for a round body, by the movement of which a soul might transport this body of hers through the ethereal breeze—as birds do through the air—by a certain push and counter-push against that breeze.

It remains, therefore, that the cause of this weakening and intensification resides in the other endpoint: namely, in the very center of the world that has been taken up, from which the distances are computed.

<margin>That the moving power is in the center of the system.</margin>If, therefore, the elongation of the center of the world from the body of the **PLANET** provides the **PLANET** with slowness, and the approach provides speed, it is necessary that the source of the **moving power** <note>original: "virtutis motricis", the physical force Kepler believed emanated from the Sun to push the planets</note> resides in that center of the world that has been taken up. For if this is posited, the manner of the cause will also become clear. For we understand from this that the **PLANETS** are moved almost by the principle of a balance or lever. For if the **PLANET**, the further it goes from the center, is moved with more difficulty (certainly more slowly) by the power of the center, then indeed it is just as if I were to say that a weight, the further it moves out from the <term>hypomochilio</term> <note>original: "hypomochilio", the Greek-derived technical term for the fulcrum or pivot point of a lever</note>, is rendered "heavier"—not by itself, but because of the power of the supporting arm at this distance. For on both sides—here in the balance or lever, and there in the motion of the **PLANETS**—this weakness follows the proportion of the distances.

<margin>That the Sun is in the center of the planetary system.</margin>But as to which body is in the center: whether none, as in **COPERNICUS** when he calculates, and in **TYCHO** in part; or the **EARTH**, as in **PTOLEMY** and **TYCHO** in part; or finally the **SUN** itself—which pleases me, and also **COPERNICUS** when he is speculating <note>Kepler distinguishes between Copernicus's mathematical models and his physical intuition</note>—this I began to discuss with physical reasons in the first part. For there I placed among the number of principles that which has now, in Chapter 32, been demonstrated professionally and geometrically.

<summary>Kepler argues that the physical cause of a planet's variable speed must reside in the center of its orbit rather than in the planet itself, comparing the mechanism to a physical lever. He identifies the Sun as this central source of "moving power," marking a shift from pure geometry to celestial physics.</summary>

<keywords>moving power, lever, fulcrum, animal force, Sun, Tycho Brahe, Copernicus, planetary motion, distance-speed relationship</keywords>

# PART THREE

...it has been established: that a <term>PLANET</term> moves weakly when it departs from the point from which its eccentricity <note>The degree to which an orbit deviates from a perfect circle</note> is calculated.

<margin>CHAPTER XXXIII.</margin>
From this principle I have argued with probability that the <term>SUN</term> is more likely to be in that point and center of the <term>WORLD</term>—or, for <term>PTOLEMY</term>, the <term>EARTH</term> is—rather than some other point void of any body. Let it therefore be permitted even in this chapter, now that our principle has been demonstrated, to repeat that same probable argument. Next, you will remember that I demonstrated in the second part that the phenomena during the oppositions of the nights <note>When a planet is directly opposite the Sun in the sky, a key time for observation</note> follow beautifully if we take the oppositions of <term>MARS</term> with the apparent <term>SUN</term> into consideration; by doing so, we construct both the eccentricity and the distances from the center of the <term>SOLAR</term> body itself. Thus, the <term>SUN</term> itself once again comes to be the center of the <term>WORLD</term> (according to <term>COPERNICUS</term>) or at least the center of the <term>PLANETARY SYSTEM</term> (according to <term>TYCHO</term>). 

But of these two arguments, one rests on physical probability; the other proceeds from "what is possible" to "what is." Therefore, I have deferred a third argument until Chapter 52, because of the difficulty of comprehension, to demonstrate from observations that it cannot happen otherwise: we must refer the <term>PLANET MARS</term> to the apparent positions of the <term>SUN</term> and draw the diameter of the apsides <note>The line connecting the closest and farthest points of an orbit</note>, which bisects the eccentric, through the body of the <term>SUN</term> itself—unless perhaps we wish to admit such an eccentric that is by no means tolerated by the parallaxes of the <term>ANNUAL ORBIT</term> <note>The apparent shift of a star's position as seen from opposite sides of Earth's orbit</note>. Let whoever bears the delay impatiently read Chapter 52 on this matter; and having read it, let him finally proceed with reading here. For nothing is assumed there except pure observations. You will find a similar demonstration in the fifth part, based on the ratios of latitudes.

<margin>The motive power is in the Sun.</margin>
With the **SUN** therefore coinciding with the center of the **SYSTEM**, the source of the motive power—based on what has now been demonstrated—coincides with the **SUN**, since it has just now been found in the center of the world.

Indeed, if I had undertaken to demonstrate this very thing—which I have now demonstrated *a posteriori* <note>original: "a posteriori"; reasoning from observed effects to causes</note> (from observations) through a somewhat long deduction—if, I say, I had undertaken to demonstrate it *a priori* <note>original: "a priori"; reasoning from theoretical principles or the nature of the object</note> (from the dignity and excellence of the **SUN**): that the same body which is the source of the world's life (which life is seen in the motion of the stars) is also the source of light, by which the adornment of the whole machine consists, and likewise of the heat, by which all things are quickened; I think I would have deserved to be heard with favorable ears.

<margin>That the Sun is in the center of the world, and does not move from place to place.</margin>
But let **TYCHO BRAHE** himself see, or whoever it is who prefers to follow his general hypothesis of the "second inequality" <note>The component of planetary motion caused by the Earth's own movement (or the Sun's movement in Tycho's system)</note>, by which, with a semblance of truth, this physical harmony is accepted for the most part (for even to them, through the use of the apparent position of the **SUN**, the **SUN** falls back into the center of the **PLANETARY SYSTEM**)—let them see how they might again repel it from their hypothesis in one respect.

For from what has been said, it appears that one of two things must follow: either that the power residing in the **SUN**, which moves all the <term>PLANETS</term>, also moves the <term>EARTH</term>; or that the **SUN**, and the <term>PLANETS</term> linked to it through its motive force, are carried around the <term>EARTH</term> by some power that resides in the <term>EARTH</term>.

For **TYCHO** himself destroyed the reality of the <term>ORBS</term> <note>The ancient idea of physical crystalline spheres carrying the planets</note>; in turn, I have invincibly demonstrated in this third part that there is an equant <note>A mathematical point used to explain why planets seem to speed up or slow down</note> in the theory of the <term>SUN</term> or the <term>EARTH</term>. From this it follows that if the <term>SUN</term> itself is moved, its motion is intensified and relaxed according as it is nearer or farther from the <term>EARTH</term>, and thus it would follow that the **SUN** is moved by the <term>EARTH</term>. But if the <term>EARTH</term> is moved, it too will be moved by the **SUN**, and that faster or slower as it is nearer to it...

CHAPTER XXXIII.

...or it has become more distant from it: while the power residing in the body of the <term>SUN</term> <note>Kepler calls this "virtus motrix," a magnetic-like force he believed the Sun used to push planets</note> remains perpetually constant. Therefore, between the two options already proposed, there is no middle ground. I rest in <term>COPERNICUS</term> <note>The astronomer who proposed the Sun-centered model</note> and allow the <term>EARTH</term> to be one of the <term>PLANETS</term>.

<margin>
The Moon is driven around by the Earth but not the Sun or the others; however, the Earth is driven by the Sun.
</margin>
And although the same objection can be raised against <term>COPERNICUS</term> regarding the <term>MOON</term> as I raised against <term>TYCHO</term> <note>Tycho Brahe, who argued for a stationary Earth with the Sun orbiting it and planets orbiting the Sun</note> regarding the five <term>PLANETS</term>; namely, that it seems absurd for the <term>MOON</term> to be moved by the <term>EARTH</term>, and furthermore to be linked and coupled to it, so that as a secondary matter the Moon itself is also snatched around the <term>SUN</term> by the <term>SUN</term>: nevertheless, I prefer to permit one <term>MOON</term>—related to the <term>EARTH</term> in the disposition of its body (as I demonstrated in the <term>Optics</term> <note>Refers to Kepler’s 1604 work, *Astronomiae Pars Optica*</note>)—to be moved by the power residing in the <term>EARTH</term>, which is extended toward the <term>SUN</term> (as will be said shortly in chapter 37), than to transcribe the motions of the <term>SUN</term> and all the <term>PLANETS</term> coupled to it to that same <term>EARTH</term>.

<margin>
The kinship of the Solar moving power with light.
</margin>
BUT LET US PROCEED in the contemplation of this moving power residing in the <term>SUN</term>, and now let us further see its most close kinship with light.

*For because the perimeters of similar regular figures, and thus also of circles, are to each other as their radii; therefore, as <term>alpha-delta</term> is to <term>alpha-epsilon</term>, so is the circumference of the circle described through <term>delta</term> from <term>alpha</term> to the circumference of the circle described through <term>epsilon</term> from the same <term>alpha</term>. But as <term>alpha-delta</term> is to <term>alpha-epsilon</term>, so is the strength of the power at <term>epsilon</term> to the strength of the power at <term>delta</term> inversely, through what was demonstrated in chapter XXXII. Therefore, as circle <term>delta</term> is to the narrower circle <term>epsilon</term>, so is power <term>epsilon</term> to power <term>delta</term> inversely: that is, the more spread out the power, the weaker it is; and conversely, the more concentrated, the stronger.*

From this we understand that there is just as much power in the whole circumference of the circle through *delta* as in the circumference of the narrower circle through *epsilon*: which was clearly demonstrated in the first chapter of the <term>Optical</term> part of Astronomy in the same way regarding light.
*Therefore, light and the moving power from the <term>SUN</term> agree everywhere in all attributes.*

<margin>
Whether light is the vehicle of the moving power.
</margin>
And although this light of the <term>SUN</term> cannot be the moving power itself; let others see, however, whether light behaves as an instrument or perhaps some kind of vehicle which the moving power uses.
To be sure, these things seem to contradict: First, light is blocked by opaque objects; therefore, if the moving power had light for its vehicle, a state of rest for the movable bodies would follow upon darkness <note>Meaning planets would stop moving during an eclipse if light were the only thing pushing them</note>. Again, light flows out in straight lines orbicularly <note>In all directions, like a sphere</note>, the moving power indeed in straight lines but circularly; that is, it strives into only one region of the world from west to east, not against it, not to the poles, etc.

<meta>catchword: But re-</meta>

<summary>Kepler adopts the Copernican system, arguing that the Sun's "motive power" operates similarly to light, weakening as it spreads over larger circumferences. He notes, however, that while light and motive power share geometric properties, they differ because motion is not blocked by shadows and only acts along the plane of the planetary orbits.</summary>
