### PART THREE. 171

But perhaps we will be able to respond to these objections in the chapters immediately following.

<margin>
CHAPTER XXXIII.
</margin>

<margin>
The moving power is an immaterial <term>species</term> of the Solar body.
</margin>

Finally, since there is as much power in a wide and more distant circle as in a narrow and nearby one, nothing of this power is lost on the journey from its source; nothing is scattered between the source and the movable body. Its efflux <note>A flowing out or emanation</note>, therefore, just like that of light, is immaterial. It is not like odors, which involve a loss of substance, nor like heat from a glowing furnace, or anything similar which fills the surrounding medium. It remains, therefore, that just as light, illuminating all earthly things, is an immaterial <term>species</term> <note>Kepler uses the term "species" to mean an immaterial "likeness" or representation of an object that transmits its properties through space</note> of that fire which is in the body of the **SUN**: so this power, embracing and carrying the bodies of the **PLANETS**, is an immaterial species of that power which resides in the **SUN** itself, a power of inestimable vigor, and thus the <term>first act</term> <note>original: "actus primus." In Scholastic philosophy, this refers to the fundamental capacity or inherent energy for motion</note> of all worldly motion.

<margin>
This species is understood to fall under the second type of continuous quantity; and is a certain surface.
</margin>

**THEREFORE**, since this species of power (about which I wrote in Part 1 of my *Optical Astronomy*) cannot be considered as being scattered through the intervening space between the source and the movable body, but rather as being collected at the movable body—specifically as much of the circumference as is occupied by that body—this power (or species) will not be some kind of geometric solid. Instead, it is like a certain surface, exactly like light. Thus, this is a universal law: the species of things descending immaterially do not, by the act of descending, extend through the dimensions of a body, even though they arise from a body (as this power arises from the body of the **SUN**). This is surely by the law of the emanation itself, which is not bounded by itself; however, as surfaces of things to be illuminated make it so that light is considered as a kind of surface because they receive and terminate its flow, so the bodies of the things to be moved seem to make it so that this moving power is considered as a kind of geometric body. This is because by their entire physical bulk they terminate or receive this flow of the moving species; thus, it can exist or subsist nowhere in the whole world except in the bodies of the movable objects themselves, and it is not "made" in the space between the source and the movable body, but exists there only as if it had passed through, just like light.

<margin>
How the immaterial species of the Sun's body receives quantities.
</margin>

**AND** at the same time, an objection can be answered here. For it was said in the previous sections that this moving power is extended through the spaces of the world, and is in some places more spread out and in others more concentrated, which conditions are followed by the intensification and slowing of the motion of the **PLANETS**. Yet now it has been said that this power is an immaterial species of its source, and is not received anywhere except in the movable subject, such as in the body of a **PLANET**. These things seem to conflict: to lack matter, and yet to be subject to geometric dimensions; to be spread through the vastness of the world, and yet to be nowhere except where the movable body is.

**THE ANSWER** is as follows: although the moving power is not something material, because it is nevertheless destined for matter—that is, for carrying the body of a **PLANET**—it is not free from geometric laws, at least on account of this material action of transport. There is no need for many words. For we see that these motions are completed in space and time, and that this power emanates and spreads from its source through the spaces of the world; all of which are geometric things. Why then should this power not also be subject to other geometric necessities?

<margin>
CHAPTER XXXIII.

<margin>
A comparison of light and the motive power regarding the quantity received:
</margin>
And lest I seem to philosophize too insolently, I shall propose to the reader a truly genuine example of light, since it nestles in the body of the **Sun** itself, and from there, as a companion to this motive power, it flashes out into the whole world. Who, I ask, would say that light is something material? Yet it performs its operations by reason of place, and undergoes mutual interaction: it is reflected and refracted, and it takes on quantities, so much so that it can be dense or rare, and can be considered as a surface where it is received by some illuminable object. For as was said in my *Optics*, light also, just like this motive power, **is not** in the space intermediate between the source and the illuminated object, even if it has passed through it, but was there as if it **had been**. <note>Kepler is struggling with the concept of "action at a distance." He argues that light and the Sun's force don't "fill" the air like a fluid, but are instantaneous transmissions that only manifest when they hit a physical object.</note>

<margin>
And the cause of time.
</margin>
And although light itself flows out without time <note>Kepler believed light traveled instantaneously</note>, while this power moves things in time: nevertheless, if you weigh it correctly, the logic for both is clearly the same. Light performs its functions in a moment; where matter is involved, it too progresses in time. It illuminates surfaces in a moment because here there is no need for matter to suffer anything, since all illumination is completed by reason of surfaces or quasi-surfaces, not by reason of bulk insofar as it is bulk. On the contrary, light bleaches colors over time; because here it acts on matter as matter, and heats it, driving out the contrary cold fixed in the matter of the body, not just on the surface. Exactly so also this moving power is present there from the **Sun** perpetually and without an interval of time wherever there is a suitable movable body, because it receives nothing from the movable body in order to be present. However, it moves things in time because the movable body is material.

<margin>
Why the Planets do not match the speed of their mover, the immaterial species of the Sun.
</margin>
Or if it seems right, set up the comparison in this way: that just as light relates to illumination, so it is certain that power relates to motion. Light does everything that can be done for maximum illumination, yet it does not achieve a state where color is maximally illuminated. For color confuses its own diverse species with the illumination of light and creates a third thing. In the same way, the moving power is not delayed in ensuring the **Planet** has as much speed as the power itself has; but the speed of the **Planet** is not therefore so great, either because of an intervening resistance—namely, whatever the matter of the ethereal air may be—or because of the movable body's own disposition toward rest <note>original: "dispositione mobilis ipsius ad quietem." This is a foundational description of what we now call inertia—the inherent resistance of an object to being moved.</note> (others would say weight, which I do not approve of, not even when discussing the **Earth**); from the tempering of these things with the efforts of the motive power, the periodic time of the **Planet** is produced.

## CHAPTER XXXIV.
### That the body of the SUN is Magnetic, and rotates in its own space.

**W**e have therefore spoken of that power which closely reaches and pulls the bodies of the **PLANETS**, how it is composed, how it is related to light, and what it is in its Metaphysical being. It follows that, with this flowing species as a guide (as if archety... <note>original: "archety-", catchword for the next page's "archetypus"</note>

### PART THREE

<page-num>173</page-num>

<margin>
CHAPTER 34.
</margin>
...archetype) let us contemplate the even deeper nature of the source itself. For it might seem that something divine is hidden within the body of the **SUN**, something comparable to our own soul, from which flows that <term>emanation|Kepler uses the word "species," meaning an immaterial form or likeness of the source's power</term> that drives the **PLANETS** around. This would be much like how, from the soul of a person throwing stones, a "species of motion" clings to the stones, carrying them forward even after the thrower has pulled his hand away from them. However, as we proceed more cautiously, slightly different thoughts will be supplied to us.

<margin>
That the power which moves the planets rotates.
</margin>
FOR BECAUSE that power, stretched out from the **SUN** to the **PLANETS**, moves them in a circle around the unmoving body of the **SUN**, this cannot happen—nor can it be understood by thought—in any other way than this: the power itself travels the same path along which it drags all the other **PLANETS**. This can be seen in part in catapults and all violent motions. In this way, *FRACASTORO* <note>Girolamo Fracastoro (1478–1553), an Italian physician and astronomer</note> and others, following the reports of the most ancient Egyptians, would not have spoken the truth in suggesting that some of the **PLANETS**, their orbits gradually tilting beyond the poles of the world, would later travel a path contrary to the others and to their modern course. On the contrary, the bodies of the **PLANETS** are perpetually carried toward that region into which this power emanating from the **SUN** directs itself.

Since this <term>emanation|species</term> is immaterial, exiting from its body into this distant space without a delay of time, and is in all other respects similar to light; it is not only necessary from the nature of the emanation, but also probable in itself because of this kinship with light, that as it is divided along with the particles of its body or source, so too a particular part of the **SOLAR** body will always face the same region of the world as the corresponding part of the immaterial emanation which belonged to that part of the body from the beginning of creation. Unless this were the case, it would not be an "emanation," and it would fall away from the body in curved rather than straight lines.

Therefore, with the emanation moving in a circle so that it might impart motion to the **PLANETS** by that movement, it is necessary that the body of the **SUN**, or the source, moves along with it. This is not moving from place to place in the WORLD (for I have said that I, along with *COPERNICUS*, leave that body of the **SUN** in the center of the world), but moving upon its own center or axis, which remain FIXED; while its parts pass from place to place (yet within the same space, the whole body remaining).

<margin>
An example regarding light.
</margin>
So that the force of the argument from similarity might be more evident, I would like you to remember, reader, what was demonstrated in my *Optics*: that vision occurs through the emanation of "little lights" <note>Kepler's term for rays or particles of light</note> from the surfaces of the seen object into the eye. Imagine, then, some orator in a large assembly of people surrounding him in a circle, turning his face (or his whole body) once. To those listeners to whom he offers his eyes face-to-face, they see his eyes; but those who stand behind him then lack the sight of his eyes. But as he turns himself, let him carry his eyes around to everyone in the circle. Thus, in the success of a very short time, everyone enjoys the sight of his eyes. Yet they enjoy it through the arrival of the "little light," or the emanation of color, falling from the orator's eyes into the eyes of the spectators. Therefore, by turning his eyes around in that narrow space in which his head is located, he simultaneously carries the rays of that "little light" around in that very wide circle in which the spectators' eyes are arranged all around.

<summary>Kepler argues that for the Sun's power to move planets in a circle, the Sun itself must rotate on its axis, using an analogy of an orator turning his head to make eye contact with a surrounding crowd.</summary>

<meta>Continuing from page 173, Kepler continues Chapter 34. He has been arguing that the Sun's motive power is an immaterial emanation. Now, he uses a logical analogy to prove that for this power to rotate and move the planets, the physical body of the Sun itself must be rotating.</meta>

<page-num>174</page-num>
<header>ON THE MOTIONS OF THE STAR MARS</header>

<margin>CHAPTER 34.</margin>
Unless that little light <note>Kepler is likely referring to an optical experiment or a physical model where a beam of light is cast from a source; if the spot of light moves, the source must be turning.</note> circled around as one, those watching it would not see its various appearances. Here you see clearly that an <term>immaterial species|an intangible "form" or likeness of a thing, such as light or a magnetic force, that carries the properties of its source through space</term> of light is either rotated or stands still along with its source—the thing to which the species belongs—whether that source is rotating or standing still.

<margin>That the Sun rotates.</margin>
SINCE THEREFORE the species of the source, or the power moving the **PLANETS**, rotates around the center of the world, I conclude (not at all absurdly, based on the example just mentioned) that the thing itself to which the species belongs—namely, the **SUN**—must also rotate.

This is also proven by the following argument: a physical motion that happens in a specific place and takes a specific amount of time cannot belong to a "naked" or pure immaterial species. Such a species cannot "suffer" or receive the effect of a motion thrust upon it; if this power lacks matter, any motion it receives would have to happen instantaneously, without taking any time at all. Since it has been proven that this moving power does circle around, and yet it cannot be granted infinite speed (for it would then seem to bestow infinite speed upon the physical bodies of the planets), it must take a certain amount of time to complete its circuit. Therefore, the power cannot perform this motion by itself; it is necessary that it moves only because the body upon which it depends—the **SUN**—is moving.

<margin>The natural cause of the zodiac.</margin>
And by the same argument, it seems rightly concluded that there is nothing immaterial within the boundaries of the **SOLAR** body which, by its own turning, causes this species descending from it to turn as well. For again, motion through space over a period of time is not rightly attributed to anything immaterial. It remains, therefore, that the body of the **SUN** itself rotates in the manner described above. By the poles of its rotation (a line drawn from the center of its body through its poles toward the Fixed Stars), it marks the poles of the zodiac; and by the greatest circle of its body, it defines the ecliptic. In this way, a natural, physical cause is provided for these astronomical arrangements.

<margin>That there is in the bodies of the planets a material inclination toward rest in every place where they are placed alone.</margin>
FURTHERMORE, we see that the individual **PLANETS** are not caught up with equal speed at every distance from the **SUN**, nor do they all move at the same speed at their various distances. Instead, **SATURN** weaves delays of 30 years, **JUPITER** 12 years, **MARS** 23 months, the **EARTH** 12 months, **VENUS** seven and a half months <note>original: "sesquiocto," literally "nine-eighths" or "one and an eighth." In the context of the Earth's 12 months, this ratio relates to Venus's period of roughly 225 days.</note>, and **MERCURY** 3 months. And yet, based on what was said before, every "orb" of the power emanating from the **SUN** is twisted with a rotation equal to the **SOLAR** body and in the same amount of time—this is true whether it is the part of the power reaching Mercury (the lowest planet) or the part reaching Saturn (the highest). There is nothing absurd in this, since the emanating power is immaterial; by its own nature, it could move at infinite speed if motion were applied to it from elsewhere, as it is hindered neither by weight (which it lacks) nor by the resistance of a physical medium. From this, it is clear that the **PLANETS** are "clumsy" or unfit to keep up with the speed of the motive power. **SATURN** is more "unfit" than **JUPITER** because it completes its circuit more slowly, even though the power at Saturn's distance rotates just as quickly as the power at Jupiter's distance. This continues down to **MERCURY**, who, following the example of the higher planets, will also be slower than the power that carries him. It is necessary, therefore, that the nature of the planetary globes be <term>material|composed of physical matter</term>, possessing an inherent property—present since the beginning of things—that makes them prone to rest or to the absence of motion. <note>This is a foundational description of what we now call inertia: the tendency of matter to resist changes in motion.</note>

<margin>That the motion of the Planets is a "passion."</margin>
A struggle arises from the competition between these two things: the driving power of the Sun and the material resistance of the planet. Therefore, the **PLANET** "wins" more (resists more) when it is in a place where the power is weaker, and thus it is moved more slowly; it "wins" less when it is closer to the **SUN**.

<summary>Kepler argues that because the Sun's immaterial motive power takes time to rotate, the physical Sun itself must be rotating to drive it. He also introduces the concept of material resistance (a precursor to inertia), explaining that planets move slower than the Sun's power because their physical matter naturally inclines toward rest.</summary>

# PART THREE.

<margin>
CHAPTER 34.
</margin>

From this point, analogy teaches us to establish that in all **PLANETS**, even in the lowly **MERCURY**, there exists a material force that allows them to push themselves out somewhat from the circle of the **SOLAR** virtue <note>Kepler refers to the Sun's "virtus" or power, which he envisions as a rotating force field that sweeps the planets along.</note>.

<margin>
In what amount of time the rotation of the SOLAR body within its own space is completed.
</margin>

From this it is proved that the rotation of the **SOLAR** body far outstrips the periodic times of all the **PLANETS**; therefore, at the very least, the **SUN** must rotate once in its own space in less than a three-month period.

And since in my *Mysterium Cosmographicum* <note>Kepler’s first major work (1596), where he proposed that the distances between planets were determined by the five Platonic solids.</note> I pointed out that there is almost the same proportion between the semi-diameters of the body of the **SUN** and the orbit of **MERCURY** as there is between the semi-diameters of the body of the **EARTH** and the orbit of the **MOON**; hence you might not absurdly conclude that the period of **MERCURY'S** orbit relates to the period of the **SUN'S** body just as the period of the **MOON'S** orbit relates to the period of the **EARTH'S** body. And since the semi-diameter of the **MOON'S** orbit is sixty times the semi-diameter of the **EARTH'S** body, while the period of the **MOON'S** orbit (or the **MONTH**) is a little less than thirty times the period of the **EARTH'S** body (or the **DAY**)—and thus the ratio of the distances is double the ratio of the periodic times—if this double proportion also holds for the **SUN** and **MERCURY**, since the diameter of the **SUN'S** body is about one-sixtieth of the diameter of **MERCURY'S** orbit, the time for the rotation of the **SOLAR** globe will be one-thirtieth of 88 days (which is the length of **MERCURY'S** orbit). Thus, it is probable that the **SUN** rotates in about three days.

<margin>
Whether the daily rotation of the EARTH comes from the rotation of the SOLAR globe.
</margin>

However, if you prefer to assign a daily period to the **SUN**, so that the daily rotation of the **EARTH** is managed by a certain magnetic force from the daily rotation of the **SOLAR** globe, I would not strongly object. Certainly, such a rapid rotation does not seem foreign to that body in which the first act of all motion resides.

<margin>
The MOON'S monthly motion arises from the daily rotation of the EARTH.
</margin>

This opinion (regarding the rotation of the **SOLAR** body being the cause of motion for the other **PLANETS**) is **CONFIRMED** most beautifully by this very example of the **EARTH** and the **MOON**. For because the primary and monthly motion of the **MOON**, by the force of the demonstrations used in chapters 32 and 33, comes entirely from the **EARTH** as its source (for what the **SUN** is here to the other **PLANETS**, the Earth is to the **MOON** in that demonstration). Consider, then, how our **EARTH** brings about the motion of the **MOON**: specifically, while this **EARTH** of ours, and with it its <term>immaterial species|an intangible emanation or force field that radiates from a physical body and carries its influence through space</term>, rotates twenty-nine and a half times around its axis, this emitted species has enough power over the **MOON** to drive it once around its orbit in that time, in the same direction in which the **EARTH** itself leads the way.

But this is meanwhile wonderful: the center of the **MOON** travels a line around the center of the **EARTH** in any given time that is twice as long as the path traveled by any point on the surface of the **EARTH** lying under the great circle of the equator. For if they traveled equal spaces in equal times, the **MOON** ought to have completed its circuit in sixty days, since the size of its orbit is sixty times the size of the **EARTH'S** globe.

Doubtless, such is the power of the **EARTH'S** immaterial species, and the **MOON'S** body is, without a doubt, of great rarity and weak resistance <note>Kepler suggests the Moon is "thin" or less dense than Earth, making it easier for Earth's rotating force to push it through space.</note>. Therefore, to remove any wonder, consider that based on these established principles, it would be an absolute consequence that the **MOON**—if its material force offered no resistance at all to the motion brought upon it from the outside by the **EARTH**—would be swept along with exactly the same speed as the species itself.

# ON THE MOTIONS OF THE STAR MARS

<margin>CHAPTER 34.</margin>
...with the immaterial **species** of the **EARTH** <note>In 17th-century physics, a "species" refers to an immaterial emanation or "likeness" of a body that carries its physical power through space.</note>, that is, with the **EARTH** itself, and completes its circuit in the space of 24 hours, just as the **EARTH** rotates. For although the thinness of that **species** of the **EARTH** is great at a distance of sixty semi-diameters <note>The Moon's distance from Earth is approximately 60 Earth radii.</note>, the proportion of one to nothing is the same as sixty to nothing. Thus, the immaterial **species** of the **EARTH** would overcome the entire mass <note>original: "assem", referring to the whole weight or resistance</note> if the **MOON** offered no resistance.

<margin>What is the nature of the Sun's body?</margin>
But if someone should ask me what kind of body I think the **SUN'S** is, from which this motive species descends, I command him to proceed further in this manner, led by analogy. I urge him to inspect the example of the recently mentioned magnet more closely, whose power resides in the entire body of the magnet; it grows with its mass, and is itself divided when the magnet is broken into pieces. Thus, in the **SUN**, the moving power seems so much stronger because it is likely that its body is the densest in the whole **WORLD**.

<margin>Comparison of the Solar body with a magnet.</margin>
And just as the attractive power of a magnet is spread out orbicularly <note>in a circular field</note> for the iron, so that it maintains a certain sphere within which the placed iron is attracted—yet more strongly if the iron comes closer within the embrace of that sphere—in plainly the same way, the power moving the **PLANETS** is propagated from the **SUN** into an orbit, and is weaker in the more remote parts of that orbit.

<margin>The difference between the Solar body and a magnet.</margin>
However, just as a magnet does not attract from every part, but has straight filaments (so to speak) or fibers (the seat of the motive power) extended lengthwise—such that it does not attract a small tongue of iron if it sits at the side midway between the poles of the magnet, but only directs it to be parallel to its fibers—so it is credible that in the **SUN** there is no power that attracts the **PLANETS**, as in a magnet (for they would approach the **SUN** until they were entirely joined with it), but only a directing power. Therefore, it has circular fibers stretched around in that region which is shown by the circle of the zodiac.

<margin>The reason for motion is the same in the Sun and the magnet.</margin>
Therefore, as the **SUN** turns itself perpetually, the motive power—or that outflow of the species from the magnetic fibers of the **SUN**—is also rotated into an orbit, diffused through all the distances of the **PLANETS**, and it rotates at the same time as the **SUN**. This is no different than when a magnet is moved: the magnetic power itself is also moved, and the iron follows that same magnetic power.

<margin>By the example of the EARTH it is proved that there are magnets in the heavens.</margin>
Indeed, I have touched upon a very beautiful example in the magnet, and one entirely suited to the matter; in fact, it is almost the thing itself. For why should I speak of the magnet as an example? Since the **EARTH** itself, as demonstrated by the Englishman <term>William Gilbert</term> <note>Author of *De Magnete* (1600), the first modern scientific study of magnetism, which heavily influenced Kepler.</note>, is a certain great magnet; and by the same author, a supporter of <term>Copernicus</term>, it is rotated every single day, just as I conjecture the **SUN** is rotated. And for that very reason, because it has magnetic fibers intersecting the line of its motion at right angles, those fibers surround the poles of the **EARTH** in various circles parallel to the motion. Thus, I have now rightly established that the **MOON** is carried along by this rotation of the **EARTH** and by the translation of its magnetic power, though it is thirty times slower.

<margin>Comparison of the EARTH with the SUN, as the cause of motion brought upon the Planets.</margin>
I know that the filaments of the **EARTH** and its motion mark the equator, while the circuits of the **MOON** apply themselves more closely to the zodiac; concerning this matter, see the following Chapter 37 and Part V. With this one exception, all other things agree:

## CHAPTER 35.

### Whether, just as with light, a deprivation of motion from the SUN occurs in the PLANETS due to
### OBSTRUCTION <note>original: *antiphraxis*; the Greek term for blocking or shielding one thing from another</note>.

Here I will opportunely resume the objections brought forward in chapter 33; where the mutual obscuration of the stars was first opposed to the kinship of light and moving power, and secondly, the different emanation of both species.

AND REGARDING the first point, it is worthy of consideration whether, just as one opaque body intercepts the light of the **SUN** from another, the moving bodies also impede each other in their motion when they fall on the same lines with the **SUN**: so that light might clearly be the vehicle or instrument of the moving power.

<margin>On the causes of latitudes:</margin>
For it might seem that, so this might be avoided as much as possible, the mutual inclinations of all the eccentrics, the deviations from the ecliptic, and the transpositions of the **Nodes** <note>The points where a planet's orbit crosses the plane of the Earth's orbit</note>, and even the proportions of the bodies and the thinning of shadows into a cone, were applied by **GOD**. And since it could not be completely avoided that the stars sometimes fell on the same lines as the **SUN**, it is easy to suspect that those very slow motions of the **apogees** <note>The points in an orbit furthest from the center</note> and nodes (which are like certain aberrations of the epicycles from the restorative times) drew their origin from there.
<margin>And the motion of the apsides <note>The points of least or greatest distance in an orbit</note>.</margin>

BUT THE ANSWER IS, first, that the analogy between light and the moving power must not be disturbed by rashly confusing their properties. Light is impeded by an opaque body, but it is not impeded by the body's substance itself, because of this very fact: light is light, and it does not act on a body's mass but on its surface or something like it. **Power** <note>original: *virtus*; the physical force or influence</note> acts on a body without regard for opacity. Therefore, since it is not the correlate of an opaque object, it will not be impeded by an opaque object.

On which account I would almost separate light from the moving power, were it not that I find examples in nature which, even when the rays of light are impeded, still leave their efficacy in the place they are prohibited from reaching. But I am not primarily concerned here with the association of light with the moving power.

Let us, however, take another example of the magnet to dispel this suspicion of impeded motions. Its power is not impeded at all

# CHAPTER XXXVI.

## By what measure the moving power from the SUN is attenuated through the breadth of the world.

**T**HERE FOLLOWS another objection, a little more difficult, arising from that which was opposed in the second place in chapter **XXXIIII** above regarding the kinship of light and the moving power: but which seems to fight more fiercely against our contemplation of an immaterial species, and which has long exhausted me when I was improvident.

It was **DEMONSTRATED** in chapter **XXXII** that the intensification and weakening of the **PLANETARY** motions follow the simple proportion of the distances. But it seems the power emanating from the **SUN** ought to be intensified and weakened in the duplicate or triplicate proportion of the distances or the lines of outflow. Therefore the intensification and weakening of the motion of the **PLANETS** will not be from the attenuation of the power emanating from the **SUN**. The consequence seems to be proven in this manner, as much concerning light as concerning the moving power;

### PART THREE ###

But the discussions concerning light are clearer. Let the reader understand the <term>moving power</term> <note>original: virtutem motricem. Kepler's term for the force the Sun uses to move the planets.</note> by analogy. *Initially, let there be some point $\alpha$ on the body of the <term>SUN</term>. It will therefore scatter rays in every direction: and through what has been demonstrated in <term>Optics</term> <note>original: Opticis. Kepler refers to his 1604 work, 'Astronomiae Pars Optica', where he established the inverse-square law for light.</note>, as the area of a larger spherical surface $\gamma$ bounding these rays in the imagination relates to the smaller $\beta$; so will the density of light on the narrower sphere $\beta$ relate to its density on the wider $\gamma$.*

<margin>CHAPTER 36.</margin>
*Next, let there be some great circle $\delta \epsilon$ on the luminous body of the <term>SUN</term>. Each of its points, of which there are infinite, will scatter rays into each hemisphere $\beta$ and $\gamma$ in this same proportion. And as the longer distance $\alpha \gamma$ from such a circular line (which appears straight from a distance) relates to the shorter $\alpha \beta$; so, inversely, the appearance of the circle's diameter at the shorter distance, or angle $\delta \beta \epsilon$, relates to the appearance at the longer distance, or angle $\delta \gamma \epsilon$. Since therefore this diameter appears longer from the proximity of $\beta$ than from the distance of $\gamma$ in the same proportion; and the radiation of any point is also denser from the proximity of $\beta$ than from the distance of $\gamma$; therefore, the radiation of the circle from the proximity of $\beta$ appears likely to be denser than from the distance of $\gamma$ by the <term>square proportion</term> <note>original: dupla proportione. In the mathematical language of the time, "double proportion" meant the square of the ratio ($r^2$).</note> of $\alpha \beta$ to $\alpha \gamma$.*

*Thirdly, let the visible disk itself of the body of the <term>SUN</term> be $\delta \alpha \epsilon$, and since similar surfaces (as the circular disks appear here) are in the square proportion of their diameters; and the apparent diameters of the <term>SUN</term> are in the simple inverse proportion of the distances $\alpha \gamma$ to $\alpha \beta$; therefore the circular disks will appear in the square proportion of the distances $\alpha \gamma$ to $\alpha \beta$. Moreover, since the radiation of the circle $\delta \gamma$ at $\gamma$ and $\beta$ has already been proven to be squared as the proportion of the distances $\alpha \beta$ to $\alpha \gamma$ because of its density; hence the radiation of the disk, because of its density or strength, seems to follow the <term>triple proportion</term> <note>original: tripla proportione. This refers to the cube of the ratio ($r^3$).</note> of the distances $\alpha \gamma$ to $\alpha \beta$.*

*For example, if the distances were $\alpha \gamma$ as 2 and $\alpha \beta$ as 1: the radiations of the point would be 1 at $\gamma$ and 2 at $\beta$, because of the density of light: and the apparent diameters of the circle would be 1 at $\gamma$ and 2 at $\beta$.*

*Therefore, the radiations of the diameter of the circle $\delta \epsilon$ would be 1 at $\gamma$ and 4 at $\beta$. But the disks are in the square proportion of the diameters. Therefore, the appearance of the disk at $\gamma$ would be 1, and at $\beta$ it would be 4: as if you were to say that the disk $\delta \alpha \epsilon$ seen from $\beta$ contains four times as many points as from $\gamma$; and each of those points shines twice as densely at $\beta$ as at $\gamma$. Therefore, by compounding the proportions, the density of the radiation of the whole disk $\delta \alpha \epsilon$ at $\gamma$ to the density of the radiation of the whole disk $\delta \alpha \epsilon$ at $\beta$ would be as 1 to 8.*

Nothing here disturbs us, that we calculate the apparent disk of the <term>Sun</term> when it is a hemispherical surface. For the proportion of equal multiples to one another is the same. Indeed, the spherical surface was demonstrated by <term>ARCHIMEDES</term> <note>Specifically in his work 'On the Sphere and Cylinder'.</note> to be four times the area of the great circle inscribed in the sphere. Therefore, in every respect, a body twice as distant at $\gamma$ than at $\beta$ seems as though it ought to shine eight times more dimly at $\gamma$ than at $\beta$, not merely twice as much. For it seems that the brightness of rays ought to be intensified by the fact that bodies appear larger as they approach, just as <term>VENUS</term> in the <term>perigee</term> <note>original: perigæo. The point in an orbit closest to the center of motion (here, the Earth/Sun system).</note> of its epicycle circumscribes a more evident shadow for bodies than in its <term>apogee</term> <note>original: apogæo. The point in an orbit furthest from the center of motion.</note>. Therefore, by the power of the comparison we have established between light and the <term>moving power</term>, the same things ought to be conceived regarding the <term>moving power</term> as well.

# ON THE MOTIONS OF THE STAR MARS

<margin>CHAPTER 36.</margin>

To this objection, I respond solidly that a falsehood is assumed in the first premise regarding the point. For although I spoke this way in my <term>Optics</term> <note>Johannes Kepler's 1604 work *Astronomiae Pars Optica*, where he laid the foundations for the inverse-square law of light.</note>, remember that I was speaking to students of optics, whose points and lines are not entirely indivisible. Indeed, as far as a point is concerned, since it possesses no quantity, yet radiations are amplified with the quantities of bodies, it follows that the radiation of a point is nothing in itself; therefore, where there is no radiation, there is also no greater or lesser density. Thus, the first use of the proportion of distances $\alpha\beta$ to $\alpha\gamma$ fails in this way.

Rather, for that very reason, we say that a certain point shines more strongly or weakly because that point represents to us a greater or smaller quantity.

In the second premise regarding the circle, and the third regarding the disk, two falsehoods are present. First, that a mathematical circle, lacking width, is imagined to shine: since it cannot shine of itself any more than a point can, from whose movement the circle is understood to be created. Truly, you have advanced no further toward a surface by assuming a line of three <term>stadia</term> <note>An ancient Greek unit of distance, roughly 600 feet.</note> than one of three feet.

Second, it is imagined that the optical amplification of the diameter or disk adds to the strength of the rays, when it is merely a deception of the visual faculty, belonging to the class of <term>rational entities</term> <note>Things that exist only in the mind or through perception, rather than having a physical existence.</note>, which have no physical effect. Therefore, while the circle $\delta\epsilon$ remains the same in reality—the same surface $\delta\alpha\epsilon$ (in the matter of light) and the same body $\delta\epsilon$ (in the matter of power)—whether it is viewed from $\gamma$ or from $\beta$, it will perpetually perform and achieve the same thing. It will scatter just as much power or light into the wider orb $\gamma$ as into the narrower orb $\beta$. For nothing is lost on the journey; the <term>species</term> <note>original: species. In 17th-century physics, this referred to the "form" or "image" of an object that travels through space to influence another body.</note> arrives entirely intact, however far away it may be. It is only thinned by the expansion of the spheres, so that at individual points of the spheres—say, at $\gamma$ and $\beta$—it becomes thinner at the former and denser at the latter, in the inverse proportion of the distances $\alpha\beta$ to $\alpha\gamma$. And this is the sole cause of the weakening, not the "fading away" of the source $\delta\epsilon$, which in truth does not happen except through a deception of sight.

Indeed, if it were pleasing here to argue from <term>Euclid's Optics</term> <note>The ancient Greek mathematician Euclid's work on the geometry of vision.</note>, less light comes to the nearby point $\beta$ than to the remote point, on the grounds that at $\beta$ a smaller circle bounds the hemispherical view of the luminous body $\delta\epsilon$ than at $\gamma$. Thus, not as large a portion of the **SUN** $\delta\epsilon$ can be seen from $\beta$ as from $\gamma$. But this is clearly imperceptible, and can hardly be expressed even with enormous numbers.

Truly, now that I have answered myself on this point, I laugh at my own miserable anxieties arising from this darkness.

**BUT THE OBJECTION** can be turned back in the opposite direction, as follows: If there is as much light scattered in a wide sphere as there is collected in a narrow one, there will not be as much power in both places. This is because power is considered not in a sphere, circling around like light, but in that circle in which the **PLANET** travels. For even the magnetic filaments of the **SUN** were assumed above to be stretched out in length only, and not also toward the poles or elsewhere.

**THE ANSWER IS** that the cause of light and the moving power is clearly the same, and the deception lies in the reasoning. For just as in light, there is no outflow—

# PART THREE

Q

<margin>CHAPTER 36.</margin>Rays flow out from the points and circles of the solar body to the corresponding points and circles of the sphere. For instance, at point $\gamma$, the light does not come from point $\alpha$ alone (for in that case, no density could be ascribed to the light in the surrounding spheres, since it would have no quantity at its very source, descending as it does from a single point). Instead, rays flow from the entire luminous hemisphere to every individual point of the imagined spherical surface. Thus, at point $\gamma$, a ray flows from $\delta$ just as it does from $\varepsilon$. This same principle holds true in the matter of the moving <term>virtue</term> <note>original: "virtutis." Kepler uses this term to describe a physical power or force-like influence emanating from the Sun.</note>. For although the magnetic filaments of the SOLAR body are arranged according to the length of the zodiac—and although only a single great circle of the SUN’S body lies directly beneath the zodiac or the <term>ecliptic</term> <note>The apparent path of the Sun across the sky; the plane of the Earth's orbit.</note> and as close as possible to the orbit of the PLANET—and finally, although other smaller circles (eventually tapering to the narrowness of a point at the poles) are subordinate to their corresponding circles in the sphere of the PLANET; nevertheless, from all the filaments of the SOLAR body (those standing on one hemisphere of that body), rays flow down and converge. They meet at every single point of a PLANET'S path, as well as at the very poles hanging over the poles of the SUN’S body. The body of the PLANET is carried along according to the measure of the density of this entire <term>species</term> <note>original: "specie." In Kepler’s physics, the "immaterial species" is the form or power transmitted through space that physically moves the planets.</note>, which is composed of all these filaments together.

<margin>Why Planets always remain near the zodiac.</margin>BUT IT DOES NOT follow from this that just as the SUN shines equally in every direction, the PLANET would also be moved in every direction without distinction—a result you might fear. For the magnetic filaments of the SUN do not move when considered in isolation; rather, they move insofar as the SUN, rotated very rapidly in its own space, also carries the filaments around with it, and with them, the moving <term>species</term> emanating from them. Therefore, the PLANET will not move in the opposite direction, because the SUN is perpetually rotated forward. Nor will the PLANET go toward the poles (even though some <term>species</term> from the body of the SUN is present at those points), because the filaments of the SOLAR body are not extended toward the poles, nor is the SUN rotated toward that region, but rather toward the direction where its own filaments invite it.

THESE THINGS being established, it is so far from the case that the PLANETS are snatched toward the poles that, instead, there is only one region of the zodiac, midway between the poles, through which it is necessary for all PLANETS to travel in length without any deflection, if they were to cease their own individual motions (about which see chapter 38). *For where the* SOLAR *hemisphere’s species stands near some point of the zodiac—say, in the present diagram, point $\zeta$—it consists entirely of semicircular filaments all tending in the same direction, such as from $\vartheta$ through $\varkappa$ to $\iota$, or from $\lambda$ into $\mu$, and so on. But when you move toward the poles of the world, as at point $\eta$, then—since the other pole of the* SUN’S *body, $\nu$, and the complete small circles of filaments $\lambda\mu$ that surround the pole $\nu$ are brought into view at the perspective of $\eta\nu$—the species will be composed of filaments tending in opposite directions. For the opposite parts of the circles $\lambda$ and $\mu$ move in contrary directions. Therefore, that species $\vartheta\eta\nu$, having slipped toward the poles, is less fit for inducing motion in the* PLANETS.

# CHAPTER 37.

## How the power moving the Moon is constituted.

**A**ND BECAUSE in Chapter 34 I happened to mention the motion of the **MOON** in passing; I wish to outline the whole matter a little more clearly, so that no doubt raised by the **MOON** might trouble the reader throughout this entire treatise, hindering them from readily giving me their assent. On the contrary, I hope the reader will be wonderfully strengthened by a most evident contemplation of the **LUNAR** motion; and finally, that the Physical part of Astronomy might be made complete in this book. For although a few small matters regarding the theory of the **MOON** must be deferred, or presented differently, or explained in greater detail elsewhere, they nevertheless take their origin from here.

**TYCHO BRAHE** <note>Tycho Brahe (1546–1601), the Danish nobleman and astronomer whose precise observations formed the basis for Kepler's work.</note> noticed through long and very frequent observations of the **MOON** in every position relative to the **SUN**, that in the **MOON**, besides the <term>anomaly</term> <note>original: "anomaliam." A term for the irregularity in a planet's motion compared to a perfect circle.</note> of the <term>epicycle</term> <note>A small circle whose center moves around the circumference of a larger one; used in ancient astronomy to explain retrograde motion.</note>, and besides that monthly anomaly which was also known to **PTOLEMY**, even the <term>mean motion</term> <note>original: "motus medius." The theoretical uniform motion of a celestial body.</note> itself (so called in respect to these two inequalities) is not yet clearly "mean" or uniform. Rather, it is intensified <note>It speeds up.</note> at conjunctions and oppositions with the **SUN**, and slackened <note>It slows down.</note> in the quadratures <note>The points where the Moon is 90 degrees away from the Sun, such as the first and third quarter phases.</note>. Thus, even if the **MOON** were disturbed by no epicycles, but were simply traveling around the **EARTH** in a <term>concentric</term> <note>A path that shares the same center as the Earth.</note> orbit, it would still travel unevenly.

<summary>In this chapter, Kepler begins to apply his physical theories to the Moon, noting that Tycho Brahe's observations prove the Moon's speed varies based on its position relative to the Sun. *Let s be the body of the* **SUN**, *m the orbit of* **MERCURY**, *v of* **VENUS**, *T of the* **EARTH**, *P of* **MARS**, *etc. And let them all be moved perpetually from right to left.* <note>In the context of Kepler’s diagrams, "right to left" usually signifies the counter-clockwise motion of the planets as viewed from the north pole of the ecliptic.</note> *Furthermore, let C L O F be the orbit of the* **MOON**, *o being the* **MOON** *in opposition* <note>The position where the Moon is on the opposite side of the Earth from the Sun (Full Moon).</note>, *c in conjunction* <note>The position where the Moon is between the Earth and the Sun (New Moon).</note>, *and L and F in the quadratures* <note>The points halfway between conjunction and opposition (First and Third Quarters).</note>. *And let C L O F remain concentric, described from the* **EARTH** *at T, and be moved into the region O F C L. The question is: what is the cause for the* **MOON** *being faster around T when at c and o than when at F and L, even though we have already mentally removed eccentricity and epicycles? At this point, I know the reader expects me to say it is faster at o because its motion there occurs in the same direction as the motion of all the* **PLANETS**. *But this is not the true cause. For in that case, the* **MOON** *would become slowest at c due to the composite motion, since its own motion F C L would somewhat resist that common motion toward the left. It must be understood that the* **MOON** *in its own orbit is carried less toward the right at c than the* **EARTH** *is carried toward the left in its own orbit. Therefore, by a motion composed of its own and the* **EARTH'S** *common motion, the* **MOON** *is always carried toward the right above, when the* **EARTH** *is at δ, but here, when the* **EARTH** *is lower at τ, it is carried toward the left; yet it moves slowly around c and quickly around o, a type of motion which the spiral lines drawn here closely express.*

*But perhaps you expect something else—that I might say this phenomenon arises because the* **SUN'S** *motive power is weaker at o and more stirred up at c? I would say this even less. For if I did, I would make it so that the Moon becomes slow at both o and c, and fast at F and L, which is the opposite of what is sought. For if it is moved weakly at o, it is therefore slow; and if it is more strongly hindered at c from tending in the opposite direction from c toward L, it will again move slowly from c toward L. Truly, it is not correct for us to allow the* **MOON** *to be free from the Earth and subject only to the Sun. For it would eventually wander away from the* **EARTH**, *just as apogees* <note>The point in an orbit farthest from the center of attraction.</note> *wander from their places. Rather, a retentive power* <note>original: "vis retentiva"</note> *must be attributed to the* **EARTH** *over the* **MOON**, *like a kind of chain; which would exist even if the* **MOON** *did not revolve around the* **EARTH** *at all. Given this power, the* **MOON** *is carried with the* **EARTH** *as if in the same ship, namely, in the same power of the* **SUN** ☉; *and now, as if it were free of this motion from the* **SUN**, *it is rotated privately by the* **EARTH**.*

*Therefore, I think there is no other cause for the speed at o and c than this: that the Earth at τ has drawn the power of moving the Moon from the Sun s, and preserves it by the continuation of the line τ s. Therefore, s c τ o can rightly be called the* <term>virtuous diameter</term> <note>original: "diameter virtuosa." From the Latin "virtus," meaning power or strength. Kepler means a line of physical influence or "empowered diameter" where the moving forces are most concentrated.</note>, *since these two sources, namely τ and s, are the origins of all motion.*

*For if this is granted, that monthly inequality known to* **PTOLEMY** *will also follow. For if the power at c and o is stronger than at F and L, having flowed from the same source τ, then if the apogee is located at c or o, there is a greater loss of speed than if the apogee were at F or L. Therefore, greater equations* <note>In astronomy, an "equation" is a correction applied to a mean motion to find the true position.</note> *result from an apogee at o or c into F and L, than from an apogee at F or L into the conjunctions and oppositions at c and o.*

*You see, therefore, that these physical speculations are so arranged that they can even suffice for the phenomena of the* **MOON**; *and that the* **MOON** *is not incited by the* **SUN** *primarily so that it circles the* **EARTH**, *but by some power hidden within the* **EARTH** *itself, which shoots out an immaterial species of itself* <note>Kepler’s term for an influence or force that radiates without taking up physical matter.</note> *to the body of the* **MOON**, *yet stronger in the line that connects the center of the* **SUN** (*the primary source*) *and the* **EARTH**.*

*How this diameter truly becomes more "virtuous" is difficult to explain more clearly. For neither the power of the* **SUN** *nor the* **EARTH** *emanating into the* **MOON**—

<summary>Kepler argues that the Moon's increased speed at conjunction and opposition is caused by a "virtuous diameter," a line of physical force created where the Earth's power is reinforced by its alignment with the Sun. He rejects the idea that the Sun moves the Moon directly in its orbit, asserting instead that the Earth's own internal power carries the Moon along while keeping it tethered.</summary>

...for it is then faster when the **MOON** falls into it. For it is most reasonable that the revolutions of these bodies (and therefore of their species <note>Kepler uses the term "species" to refer to the immaterial influence or "image" of a body's power that emanates through space to affect other bodies.</note>) are uniform and perpetually constant. It remains, therefore, only as stated: that the power <note>original: "virtus"</note> falling from the **EARTH** is not indeed faster, but rather stronger in the parts of the line $s \tau$ <note>This line represents the vector connecting the Sun and the Earth.</note> that are nearer [to the Sun]; this is because it is originally derived through that very line from the **SUN** into the **EARTH**.

Moreover, that the **SUN** is the primary director of that motion which the **EARTH** imparts to the **MOON**—whether immediately or through that which provides the annual motion to the **EARTH**—is best demonstrated by this: the circuit of the **MOON** is completed under the zodiac <note>The ecliptic plane, where the Sun appears to move.</note>, just like the annual circuit of the **EARTH'S** center, even though the **EARTH'S** daily motion (which imparts the monthly motion to the **MOON**) proceeds under the equator.

## ->C H A P T E R  XXXVIII.<-

### ->That planets, besides the common motive power of the SUN, are endowed with an innate power: And that the motions of each of them are composed of two causes.<-

**I** have spoken of the origin of that motion which rotates the **PLANETS** around the **SUN** or the **MOON** around the **EARTH**; that is, of the natural causes of that circle which, according to the varying intentions of authors, is called either the eccentric or the concentric in the theories of the **PLANETS**. Now, I must also speak of the natural cause of the eccentricity itself, or, in the particular hypothesis of **COPERNICUS**, of the epicycle on the concentric. For the moving power from the **SUN** has thus far been uniform, drawing different degrees only through the different widths of the circles: its nature is such that if a **PLANET** <note>original: "PLANETA"</note> remained at the same distance from the **SUN**, it would be carried around most uniformly, feeling no intensification or lessening of the **SOLAR** motion. However, that a certain inequality <note>A variation in speed or position, often called an "anomaly."</note> has been detected in the operation of this power happens because the **PLANET** was transposed from one distance from the **SUN** to another; in this way, it falls into different degrees of strength of this power from the **SUN**. The question is therefore: if there are no solid orbs, as **BRAHE** <note>Tycho Brahe (1546–1601), the Danish astronomer whose precise observations provided the data Kepler used to prove that planetary orbs were not physical, solid spheres.</note> demonstrated, how does it happen that a **PLANET** ascends from and descends toward the **SUN**? Is this also from the **SUN**? I say: in a way it is from the **SUN**, and in a way it is not.

<margin>
The first argument from eccentricity.
</margin>
The examples of natural things and this kinship of celestial things with these terrestrial ones "tasted" <note>An idiom meaning "examined" or "sampled."</note> thus far, cry out that the more common the operations of a simple body are, the simpler they are; whereas varieties, if there are any (such as the different distance from the **SUN**, or eccentricity, in the motion of the **PLANETS**), exist from external concurring causes.

<meta>catchword: So in</meta>

<summary>Kepler concludes that the Sun is the ultimate source of the Earth's power over the Moon and begins Chapter 38, arguing that planetary eccentricity must be caused by an innate power within the planets themselves reacting to the Sun's force.</summary>

<meta>Kepler is continuing his physical explanation of planetary motion. Having established that the Sun provides a driving force, he is now using analogies of water and ferry boats to explain why planets do not move in perfect circles, suggesting they must possess an internal "rudder" or power to navigate the Sun's "current."</meta>

<page-num>189</page-num>
<header>PART THREE. 189</header>

<margin>CHAPTER 38.</margin>
Thus, in a river, the simple property of water is to descend toward the center of the <term>EARTH</term> <note>original: "TERRÆ"</note>. However, because its path is not straight, it turns aside wherever it finds a sunken bed; it stagnates where it encounters a level plain; it is swept along with a roar where it is urged by steeper gradients; and there are places where it spins into whirlpools if, in its swifter fall, it strikes against projecting rocks. In this case, the water itself, by its own innate force, strives for nothing but a descent to the center of the <term>EARTH</term>; by a simple property, it performs a simple task. Yet the turning, the stagnation, the surging, the vortices, and all the variety arise from the assigned causes, which are, as it were, external and accidental.

Particularly delightful and more suited to our business are the spectacles shown in the propulsion of ships. If a rope or cable hangs across a river, fastened to both banks, and a pulley <note>original: "trochlea"</note> running along the cable holds a boat drifting in the river by another rope; and if the ferryman <note>original: "portitor"</note> has lashed the rudder or oar in a suitable manner, while he remains still; the boat is snatched across by the simple force of the river flowing downward, and is transported from one bank to the other as the pulley runs down the overhead cable. In wider rivers, they drive boats in circles, cross back and forth, and perform a thousand tricks without touching the bottom or the shores, but by the help of the oar alone, turning the single and very simple downstream flow of the river to their own desires.

In almost the same way, the power <note>original: "virtus"</note> that goes out from the <term>SUN</term> into the world through its species <note>Kepler’s "species" is an immaterial emanation of power that moves the planets.</note> is a kind of rapid torrent, which snatches all the <term>PLANETS</term> (and perhaps even the entire ethereal air <note>original: "aura ætherea"</note>) from the west to the east. By itself, it is not fit to bring bodies toward the <term>SUN</term> or to propel them further away from it; that would be a task of infinite trouble. It is necessary, therefore, that the <term>PLANETS</term> themselves, like certain boats, have their own peculiar <term>motive powers</term> <note>original: "virtutes motrices"</note>, like certain sailors or ferrymen. By their providence, they manage not only the approaches to the <term>SUN</term> and the retreats from the <term>SUN</term>, but also (which could be a fruitful argument) they administer the deviations in <term>latitude</term> <note>In astronomy, "latitude" refers to a planet's distance north or south of the ecliptic, the Sun's apparent path.</note>. They cross this river—which by itself follows only the path of the ecliptic—as if from one bank to another, I mean from the North to the South and back again.
<margin>Second argument from latitudes.</margin>

For it is certain from what has been said before that the power which comes from the <term>SUN</term> is simple. Yet now the eccentric orbits of the <term>PLANETS</term> not only decline from the ecliptic, but also go into various regions, intersecting each other and the ecliptic. Therefore, other causes are joined to the motive power from the <term>SUN</term>.

## By what path and by what means the powers innate in the <term>PLANETS</term> must move, so that the circular orbit of a <term>PLANET</term>, as is commonly believed, may be produced through the ethereal air.

<meta>Kepler continues his physical inquiry into planetary motion. Having previously used the analogy of a ferryman navigating a river, he now formalizes his physical assumptions into six "axioms." These axioms establish his revolutionary view that planets are naturally inert and require an external force from the Sun to move, while their specific deviations from a circle (approaching or receding) come from an internal power.</meta>

<page-num>186</page-num>
<header>ON THE MOTIONS OF THE PLANET MARS</header>

## CHAPTER XXXVIII.

<margin>
Axioms for the contemplation of celestial motions.
</margin>

**L**ET these axioms, then, be held as most true among the things we have demonstrated. **FIRST**, that the body of a **PLANET** is by nature inclined toward rest in every place in which it is placed alone. <note>This is a precursor to the concept of inertia, though Kepler believed objects naturally tended toward rest rather than maintaining constant motion.</note> **SECOND**, that it is transported from place to place, according to the longitude of the zodiac, by that power which emanates from the **SUN**. **THIRD**, if the distance of the **PLANET** from the **SUN** did not change, the path resulting from this transposition would be circular. **FOURTH**, for the same **PLANET** remaining at two alternating distances from the **SUN** for a full circuit, the periodic times would be in double proportion to the distances or the width of the circles. <note>original: "dupla proportio." Kepler is suggesting that the time it takes to complete an orbit is directly proportional to the distance, an idea he would later refine into his Third Law (Harmonic Law).</note> **FIFTH**, the raw and solitary power residing in the body of the **PLANET** itself is not sufficient for transporting its body from place to place, since it lacks feet, wings, and fins with which it might push against the ethereal air. **SIXTH**, and yet, the approach of the **PLANET** toward the **SUN** and its recession from it arise from a power that is proper to the **PLANET**. All these points are both consistent with nature in themselves and have been demonstrated up to this point.

<margin>
**I.**
What does the Planet aim for by the motion of its body while a perfect circle is created from its composite journey? That is, what kind of distances from the **SUN** does it aim for?
</margin>

Now let us practice with geometric figures, so that it may appear by what laws we must represent any orbit of a **PLANET**. Let the orbit of the **PLANET** be a circle, as has been believed until now, and let it be eccentric to the **SUN**, the source of power. Let that eccentric circle be $CD$, described with center $B$ and radius $BC$: in this, $BC$ is the line of apsides <note>The line connecting the points where a planet is closest to and farthest from the sun.</note>, $A$ is the **SUN**, and $BA$ is the eccentricity. Let the eccentric be divided into any number of equal parts, beginning from the line of apsides at $C$: let the ends of these parts be connected with $A$. Therefore, $CA, DA, EA, FA, GA, HA$ will be the distances of the ends of the equal parts from the source of power. Now, with center $\beta$ and radius $\beta\gamma$, which is equal to $AB$ itself, let an epicycle <note>A small circle whose center moves along the circumference of a larger circle.</note> $\gamma\delta$ be drawn, divided into as many parts equal to each other as the eccentric, beginning from $\gamma$: and let the line $\gamma\beta$ be continued so that $\beta\alpha$ equals $BC$: and let point $\alpha$ be connected with the ends of the equal parts of the epicycle by the lines $\gamma\alpha, \delta\alpha, \varepsilon\alpha, \zeta\alpha, \eta\alpha, \vartheta\alpha$: these lines will be equal, in order, to the distances constructed from $A$ in the eccentric. Indeed, this was demonstrated above in the second chapter. Therefore, with center $\alpha$ and radius $\delta\alpha$, let an arc $\delta\vartheta$ be drawn cutting the diameter $\gamma\zeta$ at $\lambda$: and let the ends of the parts equally distant from the aphelion <note>The point in the orbit farthest from the Sun.</note> $\gamma$ of the epicycle be connected by the lines $\delta\vartheta, \varepsilon\eta$, which cut the same diameter at the marks $\kappa, \mu$, so that $\alpha\delta$ or $\alpha\iota$ is longer than $\alpha\kappa$, and $\alpha\varepsilon$ or $\alpha\eta$ is longer than $\alpha\mu$.

<margin>
The first method: that the Planet itself traverses an epicycle. Chapter 49 almost entirely relies on this method.
</margin>

Now, if it were possible for a **PLANET** to travel a perfect epicycle by its innate force, and at the same time for its orbit to be a perfect circle, then one would have to imagine similar arcs being completed simultaneously in both the eccentric and the epicycle. Thus, it would immediately be clear by what means and by what measure this would be achieved.

<summary>Kepler outlines six fundamental physical axioms for planetary motion, asserting that while the Sun drives the planets around their orbits, the planets themselves possess an internal power to move toward or away from the Sun. He then introduces a geometric proof using an eccentric circle and an epicycle to model these changing distances.</summary>

...the distance $\alpha\iota$ would be perceived as equal to $\alpha D$ itself. For because $\alpha\iota$ and $\alpha\vartheta$ are equal, the **PLANET** going from $\gamma$ to $\vartheta$ would necessarily, and without any special deliberation, make the distance $\alpha\vartheta$ just and equal to $\alpha D$ itself.

<margin>CHAPTER XXXVIII.</margin>
But besides the fact that this seems to conflict with the fifth axiom—which says that a **PLANET** moves from place to place from $\gamma$ to $\vartheta$ by an innate force—many other absurdities are also involved.

<margin>Absurdities of this kind. 1.</margin>
*For let a line $AN$ be drawn parallel to $BD$, and let $AN$ be equal to $BD$, and with $N$ as the center, let an epicycle* <note>An epicycle is a small circle whose center moves along the circumference of a larger one. Kepler is testing if this geometric trick can explain the physical movement.</note> *be described which will pass through $D$. Therefore, since $CD$ is a perfect circle, the same angles would be completed by the* **PLANET** *$D$ at the center of the eccentric $B$, and by $N$, the center of the epicycle, at the center of the* **SUN $A$** *(through the equivalence demonstrated in Chapter 11), while the diameter of the epicycle $ND$, which holds the* **PLANET** *at $D$, remains parallel to $AB$ with respect to its position in the heavens. Therefore, one would have to assume here the same speed for the center of the epicycle $N$ around the* **SUN $A$** *and for the* **PLANET $D$** *around the center of the epicycle $B$, so that those motions would be intensified and relaxed at the same time. And because this intensification and relaxation is caused by the greater or lesser distance of the body of the* **PLANET** *from the* **SUN**, 
<margin>2.</margin>
*the center of the epicycle, while remaining at the same distance, would be imagined to move slowly or quickly because of the* **PLANET** *being distant further or nearer from the* **SUN**.*

<margin>3.</margin>
*And although the power carrying the* **PLANETS** *is faster than all the* **PLANETS** *without exception, as shown in Chapter 34, here we would nevertheless have to suppose in our imagination a single ray of power $AN$ from the* **SUN**, *like a line, in which the center of the epicycle $N$ would perpetually remain. 
<margin>4.</margin>
This line, along with the center $N$ itself, would sometimes be slow and sometimes fast; again, this is contrary to what was said above—that the power provides the same speed at the same distance.* 
<margin>5.</margin>
<margin>This last point is avoided below in Chapter 49, while the other absurdities remain.</margin>
*Indeed, we would have to pose the* **PLANET** *evolving itself out of this imaginary ray $AN$ into opposite directions in equal times unequally, as this ray itself becomes either fast or slow.*

In this way, we would indeed draw closer to the geometric suppositions of the Ancients, but we would wander as far as possible from physical speculations, as shown in Chapter 11. Nor do my thoughts suffice for unearthing a way in which these things could happen naturally.

<margin>Second way for the Planet to construct an eccentric.</margin>
These things would be thought of more simply, therefore, if we looked at the diameter of the epicycle $ND$ remaining perpetually parallel to itself. Then, therefore, the **PLANET** would complete this motion, through the imagination not of an epicycle, but of a center of the eccentric $B$, and by maintaining itself at the same perpetual distance from that center.

<margin>Absurdities. 1.</margin>
But near the beginning of the Work in Chapter 11, it was said to be most absurd that a **PLANET** (even if you furnish it with a mind) should imagine for itself a center, and a distance from it, when there is no particular body present in that center to serve as a marker.

And although you might say that the **PLANET** looks back toward the **SUN $A$**, and already knows by heart what sort of distances from the **SUN** a perfect eccentric <note>An eccentric is a circular orbit where the center of the circle is not the same as the center of motion (the Sun).</note> ought to contain in order: first, this is too far-fetched, and it requires means that connect the effect of a perfect circular journey with the sign of the increasing and decreasing diameter of the **SUN**, even in some mind. That means, however, is nothing other than the position of the center of the eccentric $B$ at a certain distance from the **SUN**; which, as just said, cannot be done by a "naked mind" <note>Kepler argues that a planet cannot follow a mathematical point in empty space; it needs a physical reason to move.</note>.

<summary>Kepler critiques the geometric models of epicycles and eccentrics, arguing they are physically impossible because they require planets to move based on imaginary points in space rather than physical forces. He highlights the "absurdity" of a planet possessing a mind that could calculate its own distance and speed relative to an empty center of motion.</summary>

<meta>This page continues Kepler's physical and mathematical dismantling of traditional circular orbits. ### CHAPTER XXXIX.

<margin>
CHAPTER
XXXIX.
</margin>

<margin>
Absurdities.
2.
</margin>
I do not deny that a center can be conceived, and a circle around it. But what I say is this: if a center exists in thought alone, with no time and no external sign, the path of any moving body cannot be realistically arranged into a perfect circle around it.

Furthermore, if a **PLANET** derived its proper distances from the **SUN**, arranged by the law of a circle, from its own memory—deriving them from there as if from **PRUTENIC** or **ALPHONSINE** <term>Prutenic and Alphonisine tables</term> <note>These were the standard sets of astronomical data used to predict planetary positions; Kepler is mocking the idea that a planet "reads" its own instructions from a book.</note> tables—it would have to traverse equal arcs of the eccentric in unequal times, driven by an external force from the **SUN**. Thus, it would know by heart what an external and unthinking force from the **SUN** was about to effect. All of which are absurd;

<margin>
45
</margin>
Especially since, according to **ARISTOTLE**, there is no knowledge of the infinite; yet the infinite is mixed into this intensification and relaxation <note>original: "intensione & remissioni". Kepler refers to the continuous, infinitely variable speeding up and slowing down of the planet as it moves.</note>.

But it is well that the **OBSERVATIONS** themselves will not permit a perfect circle $c$ $d$ (as seen below in Chapter 44); nor do these supposedly weak speculations stand alone, and thus they are even less subject to criticism.

<margin>
Third way: that the Planet, by an innate force, is balanced on the diameter of the epicycle.
</margin>
It is therefore more plausible that the **PLANET** itself cares for nothing, neither the epicycle nor the eccentric, but that the work it performs—or concurs in performing—is a <term>libratory journey</term> <note>A "libration" is a back-and-forth movement along a straight line, like a piston or a swinging pendulum.</note> on the diameter $\gamma$ $\zeta$ tending toward the **SUN** $\alpha$.

->The question now is, by what measure does the **PLANET** measure its proper distances at any time?<-

<margin>
The measure of the libration is not sought by the PLANET from a real epicycle:
</margin>
To us, indeed, the measure is clear from **Geometry** and the diagram. *For as often as the **PLANET** is moved by the **SOLAR** force into the line $DA$, we then inquire after the angle $CBD$, and we make $\gamma \beta \delta$ equal to it. And so we say that $\alpha \delta$, or its equal $\alpha \iota$, is the proper distance of the **PLANET** located at $D$ from $A$. But we have already taken this proposed measure away from the **PLANET**, since we have reduced it from the width of an epicycle into the narrowness of the diameter $\gamma \zeta$.*

<margin>
Nor from the completed arcs of the eccentric:
</margin>
Indeed, in this inquiry, it is easier to say what it is *not* than what it *is*. For because the **PLANET**, at those moments when it was placed by the **SUN** on lines drawn from $A$ through $C, D, E, F, G, H$, is itself assumed to have produced these distances in order: $\gamma \alpha, \iota \alpha, \lambda \alpha, \zeta \alpha, \lambda \alpha, \iota \alpha$. If, therefore, the path of the **PLANET** is a perfect circle, then unequal descents of the **PLANET** on the diameter (namely $\gamma \iota, \iota \lambda, \lambda \zeta$) correspond to the equal parts of the eccentric $CD, DE, EF$. And this is in a jumbled order, such that the highest ones are not the smallest and the lowest the largest, but rather the middle ones ($\iota \lambda$) are the largest, while the extremes ($\gamma \iota, \lambda \zeta$) are smaller, and the uppermost $\gamma \iota$ is a little small—
